# Ether plugin reference

> Build EPP/1 plugins with the exact shipped manifest, SDK and host-service contracts.

Generated by go generate ./internal/plugins/devreference. Do not edit generated files.
Developer documentation and API vocabulary are in English. Capabilities describe behavior; permissions grant access. Hosted QuickJS is not Node.

## Getting started

Get a first result with [Start here in 5 minutes](/plugins/reference/five-minutes), or explore [ten authoring recipes](/plugins/reference/agent-recipes).

Build the smallest plugin that answers one useful question. Start with Plugins → Add plugin → Code, select a Studio template, and run its preview before installing. A plugin adds a source, integration, notification channel, live TV source, extension, or whole content library.

## Choose a runtime
Hosted TypeScript runs inside QuickJS on wazero. There is no Node filesystem, process, environment, or direct networking. Use the permission-checked host services. Export `handle(request)` and return `{status, headers?, body}`. Calls on the hosted `ether` global are synchronous. SDK clients may be asynchronous in a sidecar; use `await` in portable SDK code.

Remote plugins run in your own process and serve HTTP or dial an outbound authenticated WebSocket tunnel. Their OS permissions are your responsibility. A remote plugin cannot use hosted folder grants or SecretGet; configuration is delivered through the remote configuration flow.

## First hosted handler
```ts
export function handle(req) {
  if (req.path === '/ether/health')
    return { status: 200, body: { status: 'ok' } };
  if (req.path === '/ether/test')
    return { status: 200, body: { ok: true, message: 'Ready' } };
  return { status: 404, body: { error: 'Unknown route' } };
}
```

Use [Manifest](/plugins/reference/manifest) to declare identity and runtime, [Capabilities](/plugins/reference/capabilities) to declare behavior, then [Testing](/plugins/reference/testing) before distributing a package. Expand the generated declarations on each page for exact signatures, limits, and validation errors. The Go validator is authoritative where optional wire fields have conditional requirements.

## Start here in 5 minutes

Your first result is a catalogue containing The Matrix. You need an Ether development server you control, its admin token, and the Ether CLI from this checkout. No provider account or media download is needed. The sample describes a movie; playback still needs an owner-configured playable source.

## 1. Create a plugin (one minute)
From the repository root, build the CLI once if it is not already on your PATH:

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o ./ether ./cmd/ether
./ether plugin new catalogue --lang ts ./my-first-plugin
```

Open `my-first-plugin/src/index.ts` and find the `/catalog/` branch. It returns a real Stremio `metas` entry with an IMDb ID, type and name. The manifest declares the matching `featured` catalogue and a list source named Featured picks. Change the reverse-DNS plugin ID in the manifest before distributing your own project.

## 2. Get a green check (one minute)

```sh
./ether plugin check ./my-first-plugin
./ether plugin test ./my-first-plugin
```

Expect `PASS`. Errors name the field or route to fix and link to its reference topic. For an agent, use `./ether plugin check --json ./my-first-plugin`. All generated templates work without npm dependencies. The check is offline; your local server is used only in the next step.

## 3. Install and keep the loop open (one minute)
Set `ETHER_TOKEN` in your shell to your local server's admin token, then run:

```sh
./ether plugin dev ./my-first-plugin --server http://localhost:32400
```

Use your development server's actual port if it differs. Expect `Reloaded community.example.myfirstplugin` followed by `Watching`. The watcher checks conformance before installing each saved change and prints plugin logs. If a save fails, fix the reported field and save again; the watcher stays open. Ctrl-C stops it. A 401/403 means the token or grants need attention; a connection error means the server address or process needs attention.

## 4. See your result (one minute)
In that server's console, open Plugins and enable your plugin after reviewing its permissions. Open Collections → New collection. In Sources, choose Featured picks from your plugin, replacing the default catalogue source if present. Keep the media type Movies. The collection preview resolves the sample's IMDb ID to The Matrix in your Ether catalogue. If it is missing, confirm the plugin is enabled and that your development catalogue contains that title; the sample does not populate Ether's TMDB catalogue itself.

For an immediate plugin-owned page without catalogue matching, scaffold `extension` instead of `catalogue`, install it with the same dev command, then open its Language overview page from the plugin. Its ViewSpec displays the sample active language, `en`.

## 5. Make it yours and share it (one minute)
Edit the catalogue response, save, and re-open the collection preview. Keep IDs stable and page larger results. Put configuration in `settings.schema.json`, labels in `i18n/en.json`, and secrets in sealed settings rather than source. When the result looks right:

```sh
./ether plugin pack -o ./my-first-plugin.etherpkg ./my-first-plugin
./ether plugin check ./my-first-plugin.etherpkg
```

Upload that package through Plugins → Add plugin on another development server. See [the authoring recipes](/plugins/reference/agent-recipes) for ten directions to take next, [Capabilities](/plugins/reference/capabilities) for route shapes, and [Testing](/plugins/reference/testing) for the limits of offline checks.

## Recipes for humans and coding agents

Start with one useful response, then build the next thing you want to use. The guide below covers ten plugin types, exact CLI commands, manifest decisions, host-service permissions, and common repairs. Use the header’s Copy for your AI assistant button to copy all chapters and generated contracts, or give your agent `/ether/plugins/reference/llms.txt` on this server. Hosted code has no Node filesystem or npm resolution; use the shipped host-service contracts and bundle imports.

## Manifest

Every package has `manifest.json`. `id`, `version`, and `name` are required. The native `ether` block requires protocol, kind, and runtime. A manifest without that block is a plain Stremio add-on. Keep reverse-DNS identity stable and increase SemVer for updates.

```json
{"id":"org.example.hello","name":"Hello","version":"0.1.0","ether":{"protocol":1,"kind":"extension","runtime":{"kind":"hosted","entry":"plugin.js"}}}
```

## Reading the generated fields
The schema table lists required fields **within their parent object**, constraints, enum values, and explicitly declared defaults. An optional parent need not be present. Absence of a schema default does not imply zero is the runtime default: consult the Go type comments and validator below. Go field tables describe serialization, not validation requiredness. `omitempty` never proves that a field is optional for your chosen capability.

Network permissions, contribution metadata, settings references, schedules, and runtime entry points are validated together. For `ether.schedule`, the first run happens right after install (within one scheduler tick once enabled). Later runs resume from the last dispatch plus `every` across server restarts, including failed attempts; overdue entries run on the next tick. Due entries run sequentially through the existing plugin call path, including `/ether/job/` deadlines. Errors identify the field to fix. See [Capabilities](/plugins/reference/capabilities), [Settings](/plugins/reference/settings), and [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

## Capabilities & contribution routes

Capabilities describe what a plugin does; permissions describe which host data it can use. Declare only the capabilities you implement. Required contribution metadata depends on the capability and plugin kind; the generated validator below enumerates all combinations and errors.

| Capability | Entry point or contribution |
|---|---|
| stream_source | Stremio `/stream/{type}/{id}.json`; lazy streams open through `/ether/open/{id}` |
| debrid_provider | `/ether/debrid/check`, `find`, `acquire`, `link`, `remove`, `account` |
| debrid_cache_hints | `POST /ether/debrid/hints` on a viewer's Play: which listed torrents a debrid service holds |
| list_source | `contributes.listSources`; matching Stremio catalogue |
| poster_badges | `contributes.posterBadges`; `ether.badges.set`, `clear`, `usage` |
| metadata | Stremio `/meta/{type}/{id}.json` |
| plugin_directory | Plugin directory declarations and discovery routes |
| livetv_channels | `/ether/channels.json`, `/ether/guide/{id}.json`, stream routes |
| subtitles | Stremio subtitles resource; declared languages and formats |
| markers | Declared intro, credits, recap or preview marker kinds |
| notify | Notification metadata; send and send-test handlers |
| events | Event subscriptions (`POST /ether/event`) and custom published events (`contributes.events.publish`, `ether.events.publish`) |
| flow_actions | Declared Flow actions (`contributes.flowActions`) invoked via `POST /ether/v1/flow-actions/{key}` with `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key` |
| ranking_step | Deterministic `rank_key(candidate, config)` |
| rule_condition | Deterministic `cond_match(candidate, operator, value)` |
| tools | Declared tool input schema and tool handlers |
| ui | Pages, slots, commands, ViewSpec views and actions |
| onair_content / livetv_pack | Declared On Air segments or TV pack contributions |
| catalog_provider / kind_resolver / matcher | Content kind browse, resolve, match routes |
| frontend_adapter | Authenticated protocol adapter routes |

Reserved capability names cannot be claimed in EPP/1. Ranking and condition hot paths have only log and abort: no I/O, wall clock, or arbitrary host calls. Return a neutral result when there is no useful adjustment. Consult the generated templates and route checks for each response shape rather than inventing one.

## Content kinds & libraries

See the complete content-kind guide below. Start with a bounded browse page, stable external IDs, and a playable leaf. Use [Resolvers](/plugins/reference/resolvers) for bytes and [Folders](/plugins/reference/host-folders) for local files.

### Reporting a route failure

Return a non-2xx response with a body such as `{"error":{"code":"rate_limited","message":"The catalogue service is rate limiting requests","retryAfterSeconds":300}}`. Ether recognizes `auth`, `rate_limited`, `upstream_unavailable`, `not_found` and `invalid_settings`. Use one owner-facing sentence and omit credentials and URLs. Map upstream 401/403 to `auth` even if the route itself returns 502. Send `Retry-After` or a positive `retryAfterSeconds` when known. Return 501 if the optional changes route is unimplemented.

## Screens and surfaces

Give Vela a screen of your own (a sports desk, a news front page) or fill a host slot: a player overlay, an alert toast, a Home row or a title panel. You ship **documents**: JSON files in your package that Vela draws natively on TV, phone and web in the viewer's skin. The full contract is `docs/plugin-screens.md`; the document schema is `schemas/plugin-screen.v1.json`.

## Declare
Add the `screens` capability and `contributes.screens: [{id, title, icon, pages: {index: "screens/x.json"}, actions?}]` or `contributes.surfaces: [{id, presentation, anchor?, setting?, when?, document}]`. `when` may only name your own feeds and kinds.

## Write a document
`{schema: 1, kind: "screen", renderer: 19, params, sources, strings, tree}`. The tree is Vela's node language. `params` are typed page inputs; `sources` name data Ether resolves per viewer: `liveEvents`, `liveSchedule`, `liveEvent`, `liveTables`, `liveEntities`, `liveLeagues`, `watch`, `viewer` and `plugin`. Arguments may hold `{param.x}`, `{viewer.tz}` and, on surfaces, `{context.event}` style holes; never another source. Documents never contain URLs: write `asset:path` for package files.

## Answer a plugin source
```ts
p.onScreenSource("desk", "front", async ({ args }) => ({
  value: { lead: record("story", "s1") },
  records: [{ type: "story", id: "s1", value: { title: "…", hero: image("https://cdn.example.com/a.jpg"), url: link("https://example.com/s1") } }],
  maxAgeSec: 120, nextRefreshSec: 60,
}));
```
Wrap images (`image`, `asset`), links (`link`), records (`record`), events (`event`) and entities (`entity`). Ether signs images only on your `permissions.network` hosts and drops bare URL strings. `scope: "viewer"` sources receive the viewer like a frontend adapter call.

## Actions
Declare typed `actions` on the screen; answer `onScreenAction` with `{records?, sources?, refresh?, toast?, navigate?}`. Ether's own `ether.favorite`, `ether.reveal` and `ether.spoilerFree` need no code.

## Live
While a viewer has a page open, Ether re-reads it on live feed changes, on your `nextRefreshSec`, and when you call `ether.screens.invalidate()`. `ether.screens.putRecords([{type, id, value}])` patches records already on screen. Nobody watching costs nothing.

## Check
`ether plugin check` compiles every document exactly as install does and reports each problem by file and JSON pointer.

## Catalogue sources

A Stremio catalogue returns `{metas:[...]}` for `/catalog/{type}/{id}.json`. The catalogue ID must match `manifest.catalogs` and `ether.contributes.listSources[].catalog`. A list source can appear in collections and home rows; it is different from the signed **plugin marketplace catalogue** described in [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

```json
{"key":"weekly","label":"This week","catalog":"weekly","maxItems":50,"refresh":"1h"}
```

Keep pages bounded, handle search and pagination extras consistently, and use stable metadata IDs. Read parameters from the request; do not return an entire remote library to answer one query. For arbitrary media hierarchies use [Content kinds](/plugins/reference/kinds), whose provider sync persists items in Ether's store.

## Resolvers & playback

Resolve only when a viewer requests playback. Browse and metadata must stay cheap. A content-kind resolver returns ordered `sources`; an empty array means temporarily unavailable. File, range, download, direct, container, and release patterns have different ownership of fetching and caching; read the generated PlayableSource types and content-kind guide.

```json
{"sources":[{"id":"primary","pattern":"range","url":"https://media.example.org/track.mp3","mime":"audio/mpeg"}]}
```

Use `{secret:name}` header placeholders instead of returning raw credentials. URLs support only the documented integer placeholders. Return `unavailable` on kind items when an owner needs to see why verified bytes do not exist. Use Ether stream tickets for frontend adapters so media bypasses the plugin process. See [Kinds](/plugins/reference/kinds), [Source discovery](/plugins/reference/host-sources), and the native debrid route/error table below.

## Notification channels

`kind: "notification_channel"` with capability `notify` registers a delivery channel. This differs from `ether.notify.owner`, which posts a console notice. Declare `contributes.notification` with `sendTest: true`, supported formats, optional fields, and maximum length. Owners configure channel instances through Notifications.

```json
{"kind":"notification_channel","capabilities":["notify"],"contributes":{"notification":{"sendTest":true,"formats":["text"],"maxLength":1000}}}
```

Implement `POST /ether/notify` (the SDK notify handler). It receives the delivery request, including its test flag for a test send; return the documented NotifyResponse. See the generated router and conformance checks below. Validate channel fields and authenticate external delivery through declared network hosts and secrets. A successful connection test must mean the service accepted the request; do not report success after an upstream error. Never log tokens or signed delivery URLs. The Home Assistant example shows remote notification delivery.

## Styles for On Air

A plugin can be a channel style for On Air: idents, up-next cards, breaks and the rest of a channel's look, plus the artwork and fonts it uses. Style plugins run no code. Styles are shared this way; there is no separate pack format.

## The quickest way
Design the style in Live TV → Styles, then open its menu and choose **Export as plugin**. The download is a complete `.etherpkg` style plugin. Install it on another server from Plugins (upload, URL or Marketplace), or submit it to the Marketplace like any other plugin.

## Manifest
A style plugin uses the data runtime and contributes exactly one style:

```json
{
  "id": "community.style.neon-noir",
  "name": "Neon Noir",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "ether": {
    "protocol": 1,
    "kind": "extension",
    "summary": "Adds a channel style and its licensed artwork",
    "runtime": { "kind": "data" },
    "capabilities": ["livetv_pack"],
    "contributes": { "looks": [{ "id": "style", "file": "looks/style.json" }] }
  }
}
```

The rules Ether checks:
- `runtime.kind` is `data` with no `entry` or `module`.
- `livetv_pack` is the only capability.
- `contributes.looks` holds exactly one style.

## Files
- `looks/style.json`: the style document, the same JSON the Style editor saves (brand, roles, scenes, controls).
- `assets/<sha256>`: each Library image, video, audio file or font the style references by digest.
- `assets.json`: one entry per asset, with `digest`, `name`, `kind`, `license`, `mime`, and optional `source` and `attribution`.
- `digest`: the package digest. Export writes it; the CLI writes it for hand-built packages.

## Limits and licences
- One file may be at most 64 MB, and the whole package at most 128 MB.
- Fonts travel only with a licence that permits redistribution. Export swaps any other font for the bundled Inter and lists it in `warnings.json`.
- Installing the plugin adds the style to the owner's Styles, labelled with the plugin it came from. The style stays if the plugin is removed; delete it from Styles.


## Settings & setup steps

Declare `ether.settings` inline or as `{"$ref":"settings.schema.json"}`. Referenced files must be in the package. Public values come from `ether.settings.get()` per request; pooled hosted instances restart, so instance memory is not persistent configuration. Read secrets through SecretGet only in hosted code.

```json
{"fields":[{"key":"maxItems","kind":"number","label":"Maximum items"}]}
```

```ts
const maxItems = Number(ether.settings.get().maxItems ?? 12);
// POST /ether/configure validates proposed req.body:
return { status: 200, body: { errors: {} } };
```

Use `$t:key` labels with `ether.strings` and English fallback strings. Dynamic option fields should answer the SDK's options route. `contributes.setup.steps` groups settings fields and optional test routes. `/ether/v1/setup/{step}/test` receives `{step, fields}` and returns `{ok, detail, fields?}`; secrets stay out of that body. Required steps gate content-library sync and visibility until passed or owner-skipped. See the generated SetupStep and settings accessors for exact shapes.

## Events & Flows

Subscribe explicitly with capability `events` and `contributes.events.subscribe`, and handle deliveries at `POST /ether/event`. Both the 12 legacy EPP/1 event names and canonical Flows event names are supported; unknown names are rejected.

```json
{"capabilities":["events","flow_actions"],"contributes":{"events":{"subscribe":["playback.session.started"],"publish":[{"key":"scene.changed","label":"Scene changed","fields":[{"name":"scene","type":"string","label":"Scene"}]}]},"flowActions":[{"key":"set_scene","label":"Set scene","route":"/ether/v1/flow-actions/set_scene","idempotent":true,"params":[{"key":"scene","type":"string","label":"Scene","required":true}]}]}}
```

## Publishing custom events
Declare schemas under `contributes.events.publish` and emit events via `ether.events.publish(key, payload[, correlation])` (hosted) or `POST /ether/plugin-host/events/publish` (remote). Ether registers each published event as `plugin:<pluginId>/<key>`, validates payloads against the declared schema (max 64 KiB), and rate-limits publishing to 30 events/minute per plugin.

## Contributing Flow actions
Declare capability `flow_actions` and actions under `contributes.flowActions` with a route under `/ether/` and optional timeout (default 30 s, max 60 s). Ether registers each action as `plugin:<pluginId>/<key>` atomically across install, update, grant changes, and uninstall, and invokes it via `POST` with `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key` and body `{flowId, runId, nodeId, idempotencyKey, dryRun, params}`. Deduplicate side effects with `X-Ether-Idempotency-Key`, honor `dryRun`, and return `{output: {...}, branch?}`.

Keep event and action handlers bounded and idempotent. Viewer identity and secret fields are redacted per live grants. Enabled subscriptions are indexed; nobody subscribing means no plugin outbox work. See the Smart Lights example below.

## Testing & conformance

Use Studio's run and preview tools while editing. Before distributing, run the offline conformance command on an unpacked package:

```sh
ether plugin check ./my-plugin
```

The kit validates manifest fields, package references, owner-facing copy, declared routes, capability response shapes, and hot-path determinism/budgets. Content-kind checks cover pagination termination, page limits, detail round trips, declared live search, and resolver patterns. Shared kind fixtures live in `sdk/conformance/kinds`.

Mock external HTTP, store, viewer, and playback dependencies in SDK tests. Check missing grants, revoked grants, empty results, rate limits, invalid settings, and upstream failures. Offline conformance cannot prove a paid account works: after installation, run the owner's connection test with real credentials. Inspect Studio's calls and logs without exposing secrets. Package only after these checks; see [Publishing](/plugins/reference/publishing).

## Packaging & publishing

Bundle hosted SDK imports into the entry artifact. Bare package imports cannot resolve in the hosted virtual filesystem. Put the manifest, referenced settings/strings, and compiled entry into the package; do not include credentials or development caches.

```sh
ether plugin check ./my-plugin
ether plugin publish --url https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/v0.1.0/<id>-0.1.0.etherpkg ./my-plugin
```

Keep identity stable and increment version. New permissions require owner review; removing or retyping kind declarations can require explicit replacement approval. Test upgrades and the owner's rollback flow before release.

Ether reads the official signed marketplace (`https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether-plugins`, served at `https://braedonsaunders.github.io/ether-plugins/index.json`) by default under Plugins → Marketplace. Upload `<id>-<version>.etherpkg` to a GitHub release, run `ether plugin publish --url <release-asset-url> ./my-plugin` to pack the archive and print a validated `plugins/<id>.yaml` entry with its SHA-256 digest, and open a pull request against `https://github.com/braedonsaunders/ether-plugins`. Marketplace CI verifies the package digest and runs `ether plugin check` before publishing the Ed25519-signed index. Owners running their own catalogue can use the template below and set `plugins.indexUrl` and `plugins.publicKey` together.

## Troubleshooting & errors

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| Manifest rejected | Field path and validator message; capability-specific metadata; unsupported names; referenced files |
| Permission denied | Manifest declaration plus current owner grant; a grant may have been revoked since startup |
| Disabled or unavailable | Plugin enabled state, required setup, injected backend availability, saved secrets |
| Network failure | Host allowlist, guarded redirects, private-address protection, body cap, upstream status |
| Folder inaccessible | Hosted runtime, owner-picked root, relative path, symlink containment, revoked grant |
| Hash too large | Use hashStart above 256 MiB; poll until terminal; retry a busy worker later |
| SDK import unresolved | Bundle imports into the hosted entry; do not expect Node resolution in QuickJS |
| Empty library | Setup completion, sync mode, page cursors, declared levels/field types, stable IDs |
| Playback unavailable | Resolver pattern, source URL, secret placeholders, item unavailable reason, viewer access |
| Remote 401 | Plugin credential or tunnel pairing; never substitute a viewer token |
| Rate limited | Honor backoff and bounded work; owner notices allow five per hour |

Generated validators, transport error mapping, and runtime fault definitions below give the exact error messages. Search a message or field name to find its source and relevant type. Keep secrets out of diagnostic output.

## Key/value storage

Plugin-scoped string values survive instance restarts. Missing get returns null in JS; Go also returns a found flag. Use prefixes for list, and call usage() to inspect `{bytes, keys, quotaBytes, quotaKeys}` (values plus 256 bytes per key, capped at 50 MiB and 10,000 keys) before writing user state such as game saves alongside a catalogue index. Remote values are capped at 5 MiB, with the per-plugin quota also enforced. Never store secrets here.

```ts
const usage = ether.kv.usage();
if (usage.bytes + saveJson.length + 256 <= usage.quotaBytes && usage.keys < usage.quotaKeys) {
  ether.kv.put("save:slot-1", saveJson);
}
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Poster badges

Requires `poster_badges` and up to 4 sets declared in `ether.contributes.posterBadges: [{key, label, description?}]` (`key` matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$`), such as a `"dub languages"` set (`key: "dub_languages"`, `label: "Dub languages"`) for an anime plugin or an `"editions"` set (`key: "editions"`, `label: "Editions"`).

```ts
ether.badges.set("dub_languages", [
  { title: { type: "show", tmdb: 37854 }, labels: ["EN DUB", "JA"] },
]);
ether.badges.set("editions", [
  { title: { type: "movie", imdb: "tt0083658" }, labels: ["FINAL CUT"] },
]);
const usage = ether.badges.usage(); // { titles, quotaTitles }
// ether.badges.clear("editions");
```

`set(setKey, entries)` accepts up to 500 entries per call; empty `labels` deletes that title's badges in the set. At most 3 labels per title per set are allowed, each 1 to 16 characters from `[A-Z0-9 +&'./-]` (lowercase input is uppercased, anything else is rejected), up to 200,000 badged titles per plugin. Ether draws the badges itself, the owner can switch each set off in Metadata -> Artwork (`disabledBadgeSets`), and no plugin call happens while rendering.

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Public settings

Read current non-secret configuration for each request. No permission declaration is needed for your own public settings. Missing optional settings need a caller-selected default.

```ts
const count = Number(ether.settings.get().maxItems ?? 12);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Sealed secrets

Requires the exact name in permissions.secrets. `secret.get` is hosted only (remote plugins receive owner secrets via `/ether/configure`); missing or expired secrets produce unavailable, and undeclared or revoked grants produce permission denied. Both hosted and remote plugins may store plugin-derived credentials (such as session cookies or short-lived tokens) with `secret.set(name, value, ttlSec?)` and remove them with `secret.delete(name)` under declared names that are not owner-configured settings fields, then reference them as `{secret:<name>}` in playable source headers and `http.hash`.

```ts
const token = ether.secret.get("apiKey");
ether.secret.set("sessionCookie", "sid=abc", 3600);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## HTTP requests

Hosted fetch requires the destination in permissions.network or in the owner's per-plugin local network grants. Redirect destinations are checked too, and credentials or caller headers follow redirects only within the same origin, to a strict same-site subdomain (verified via the Public Suffix List, no port change or HTTPS→HTTP downgrade), or to hosts explicitly listed in `keepHeadersOnRedirect` (still within granted network hosts, never across HTTPS→HTTP downgrades, and sticky once an untrusted hop is reached). The same redirect policy applies to `http.fetchMany`, `http.fetchToCache`, `http.hash`, and playable sources (`range`, `download`, `direct`, `container`). Use `ether.http.fetchMany(requests, {concurrency?})` to overlap up to 64 independent HTTP requests on the host (bounded to 8 in-flight per batch, 6 per origin across Ether, 10 MiB aggregate response bytes, and 100 units per request); results return in input order with either `{status, headers, body, bodyBase64?}` or `{error: {code, message}}`, and parent request cancellation aborts in-flight calls. `http.hash` accepts optional `headers` with `{secret:<name>}` expansion (no hop-by-hop/framing headers, never logged or cached). Read the generated MaxFetchBytes and transport limits; private LAN destinations fail unless the owner allows the exact host or host:port under On your network in the plugin's settings (exact local names in permissions.network are pre-granted at install, while loopback requires an explicit localhost or 127.0.0.1 grant). Handle upstream non-2xx status explicitly.

```ts
const r = ether.http.fetch({url: "https://api.example.org/status", method: "GET"});
if (r.status !== 200) throw new Error("Service unavailable");

const batch = ether.http.fetchMany(
  [
    {url: "https://a.example.org/item/1", timeoutMs: 1500},
    {url: "https://b.example.org/item/1", timeoutMs: 1500},
  ],
  {concurrency: 6},
);
const ok = batch.filter((item) => !item.error && item.status === 200);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Viewers & watch state

Live viewer grants determine identity, history, and write access. Use granted() before selecting a viewer. History is bounded (host maximum 200). Watch-state writes are journalled and forbidden in read-only tool calls. Never infer authorization from a cached viewer ID.

```ts
const viewers = ether.viewers.granted();
```

Declare `viewers.write_watch_state: "granted_viewers"` and grant each target viewer. Call `ether.viewers.setWatchState({viewerId, titleId, watched})` with an owned playable `pk:<pluginId>:<kind>:<externalId>` ref or a catalogue movie or episode ID. SDK clients also accept the three positional arguments.

Subscribe to `viewer.watch.scrobbled` for manual marks and playback completions or use `viewer.watch.watched` and `viewer.watch.unwatched` to include imported current state. Subscribe to `viewer.watch.progress` for resume checkpoints in `positionMs`. The writer receives no echo from its own writes. Request `viewers.identity: "granted_viewers"` to receive the viewer ID for granted viewers.

Payloads include `titleKey`, `watched`, `state` and `source`. Sources are `playback`, `manual`, `plugin` and `import`. The optional `surface` identifies the app or writing plugin. Only the owner receives its item's `itemRef`. Catalogue events carry available `tmdbId`, `tvdbId` and `imdbId`. For episodes these identify the series and are paired with `season` and `episode`.

SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

```ts
ether.collections.upsert({id: "weekly", name: "Weekly picks", ids: []});
```

## Kind item storage & visibility

upsert/delete/items require catalog_provider and your own declared kind. upsert/delete only work for push-mode kinds; pull sync owns its writes. Push writes are journalled for undo (kept up to 30 days, 10,000 entries, or 256 MiB per plugin); unchanged items with matching content hashes are never snapshotted, and kinds may set sync.undo: "ids" to record only created and touched IDs (skipping snapshot reads, with undo deleting only created items). items is cursor-paged and unfiltered. Items are validated against declared levels and fields. Unknown custom fields are dropped; invalid types reject the item.

For frontend adapters serving their own protocol, visible and browse apply the library's Rules, library grants, and viewer content safety for the requesting viewer (same LibraryPolicy as the console and built-in projectors). Both require frontend_adapter and an authenticated frontend adapter request; non-adapter calls fail with permission denied. Viewer identity comes only from Ether's authenticated request context (and request-scoped X-Ether-Viewer-Token on remote callbacks), never guest input. visible accepts at most 500 IDs per call.

```ts
const page = ether.kinds.items("recordings", "", 50);
// Inside a frontend adapter request:
const allowed = ether.kinds.visible("recordings", ["rec-1", "rec-2"]);
const filtered = ether.kinds.browse("recordings", { query: "live", limit: 50 });
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Screens pushes

`ether.screens.invalidate()` makes your open screens and surfaces read their sources again now; `ether.screens.putRecords([{type, id, value}])` (at most 100) sends new values for your records to open screens already showing them. Both need the `screens` capability, return `{streams}` (how many open streams heard them) and do nothing when nobody is watching. Remote plugins call `POST /ether/plugin-host/screens/invalidate` and `POST /ether/plugin-host/screens/records {records}`. Go: `ctx.InvalidateScreens()`, `ctx.PutScreenRecords(...)`; Python: `host.screens.invalidate()`, `host.screens.put_records(...)`.

## Source discovery

Requires kind_resolver and sources: search, search+check, acquire, or acquire+check. Search permits indexer discovery, debrid checks, release inspection, and on-demand usenet_check; acquire permits opening content; +check additionally permits background usenet_check in jobs and schedules within the owner's per-plugin daily allowance (default 20/UTC day, configurable under Sources › Indexers › Daily budgets, answering rate_limited with retryAfterSec/retryAt once spent; on-demand viewer calls never count against it and verdicts are shared with Ether's availability/Play cache for 15 min good / 30 min bad). On viewer or deadline-bounded requests, indexer_search is deadline-aware by default: Ether caps the wait to remaining time minus max(1.5 s, 35%) (unbounded/background jobs still wait up to the 30 s ceiling), returning arrived results while stragglers finish into Ether's search cache as status: "pending". Indexers that repeatedly time out or fail enter Ether's shared circuit-breaker backoff (2 min..30 min) and are skipped immediately with status: "skipped" and reason: "paused_backoff". Optional firstResults (with settleMs, default 250 ms), minResults, skipIndexers, onlyIndexers, and timeoutMs (capped at 30000 ms and any tighter deadline reserve) further tune fan-out latency, and the response envelope includes per-indexer status in indexers: [{indexerId, indexer, status, results?, ms, reason?, error?}] (omitted for other source query kinds). Cached debrid candidates report holding services in acquisition order via cachedBy: [{id, name}] (omitted when uncached; on debrid_acquire, the service that served it). Return a release source after choosing a candidate instead of downloading in the request handler. Torrent releases follow the owner's debrid setting (queueing uncached downloads and answering preparing / 503 Retry-After when Cached torrents only is off); set release.cachedOnly: true to opt out.

```ts
const { candidates, indexers } = ether.sources.resolve({
  kind: "indexer_search",
  query: "Example",
  firstResults: true,
  settleMs: 250,
  timeoutMs: 5000,
});
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients (`kinds.resolveSources` returns candidates; `kinds.resolveSourcesWithResult` returns `{ candidates, indexers }`). See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

### Request an NZB

Use `sources.resolve({kind: "nzb_request", nzbRef})` with an opaque indexer search reference, or supply `nzbIdentity: {indexerId, guid}`. The single candidate contains a parsed `files` list, `fileCount`, and a permanent vault `nzbRef` for a playback source’s `release.nzbRef`. Ether uses the vault before spending any indexer grab. Search mirrors stable references in the deprecated fields as `ether-nzb:<nzbRef>` and `ether-torrent:<torrentRef>` for older plugins. Direct plugin HTTP calls to configured indexers are refused. Background requests require the `+check` grant and use its daily allowance.

## Library blob cache

Cache refs are content addressed blob:<sha256>, never filesystem paths. A library defaults to 2 GiB under a shared min(10 GiB, 5% of cache disk) cap; manifest and owner settings can override it. Remote blob uploads cap at 256 MiB. Call `cache.delete(blobRef)` to remove a temporary blob from your own cache namespaces and free its quota immediately so large temporaries do not evict smaller kept files; deleting an absent or already evicted ref succeeds. Use kinds for metadata and cache for bytes.

```ts
const ref = ether.cache.put("library-key", "cover.txt", "hello");
const data = ether.cache.open(ref);
ether.cache.delete(ref);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Frontend stream tickets & visibility

Mint a scoped, short-lived URL for one of your own kind items with frontend.streamURL (accepting an optional positional partIndex or { partIndex?, source?, absolute?, wait? } to pin a zero-based part, pin an exact resolver PlayableSource.id with no failover, or return an absolute URL using the request's X-Ether-Origin with fallback to the adapter's first published address), and evaluate the library's Rules and viewer access policy with kinds.visible (up to 500 IDs) or kinds.browse. Authenticated adapter requests also receive X-Ether-Origin (scheme://host[:port][/prefix], honouring trusted proxies only with inbound client values stripped) alongside X-Ether-Viewer. The authenticated viewer comes from the frontend adapter request context (and X-Ether-Viewer-Token on remote callbacks), never guest-supplied input. Embed the stream URL in the protocol response; Ether serves the bytes without proxying through your plugin. Raw hosted spelling is streamURL; the TypeScript SDK uses streamUrl.

```ts
const page = ether.kinds.browse("comic", { limit: 50 });
const allowed = ether.kinds.visible("comic", ["c1", "c2"]);
const url = ether.frontend.streamURL("item-ref");
const exact = ether.frontend.streamURL("item-ref", { source: "epub" });
const abs = ether.frontend.streamURL("item-ref", { absolute: true });
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

On adapter download routes, set wait: { maxSeconds: 1200 } to hold the media response during preparation (positive whole seconds, capped at 1800). Ether admits four held requests per plugin and 32 per server. Keep the wait below client and reverse proxy response-header timeouts. Omit wait for players to keep their 18-second default.

## Storage & folders

Hosted only. Requires folders: read and a live owner-picked root. Paths are relative to the root. Traversal, symlink escapes and revoked grants fail. list/stat return metadata, never contents. hash returns size, Unix modTime, crc32, md5, sha1. Above 256 MiB use hashStart/hashPoll/hashCancel. Only requested files are hashed; unchanged files reuse the guarded digest cache. One active job per plugin, two process-wide; jobs yield while reading and abort if the file changes. See the full kinds guide for job lifecycle and revocation.

```ts
const job = ether.folders.hashStart("picked-root", "album.flac");
const status = ether.folders.hashPoll(job.id);
// Poll later until done, canceled, or error; never busy-loop.
// ether.folders.hashCancel(job.id);
```

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Language model (AI)

Uses the owner's configured language model from Settings -> Integrations -> Language model (one AI, one connection place; never ask for a second API key). Requires `permissions.ai: "complete"` (or `"complete+search"` to also opt in to bounded, cached interactive search calls), shown on the install sheet and revocable live in plugin permissions (`ai` and `ai.search`). No model credentials, endpoint URLs, or raw provider errors ever reach the plugin.

```ts
try {
  const res = ether.ai.complete({
    messages: [
      { role: "system", content: "Extract structured search filters." },
      { role: "user", content: "90s sci-fi films without horror" },
    ],
    schema: {
      type: "object",
      required: ["genres"],
      properties: {
        decade: { type: "integer" },
        genres: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } },
        excludeGenres: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } },
      },
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
    maxTokens: 256,
  });
  // res.json is already parsed and validated against schema; res.text holds canonical JSON.
} catch (err) {
  if ((err as { code?: string }).code === "not_configured") {
    // Owner has not configured a language model: fall back cleanly.
  }
}
```

## Route policy & search opt-in
With `permissions.ai: "complete"`, `ai.complete` is allowed only on owner actions (`/ether/action/*`), background jobs (`/ether/job/*`), Flow actions (`/ether/v1/flow-actions/*`), tools (`/ether/tool/*`), event handlers (`/ether/event`), setup/test routes (`/ether/v1/setup/*`, `/ether/test`), background kind/Live TV sync, or declared `ether.schedule` routes. Precompute or cache structured results in `ether.kv` for browse/playback paths.

To use `ai.complete` during interactive search (matching Ether's own descriptive search exception), declare `permissions.ai: "complete+search"`. This adds a separate install-sheet line ("Uses your language model while a viewer searches") and an independently revocable `ai.search` grant, and opens ONLY:
- Stremio-style catalog search routes with a non-empty `search` query (`/catalog/{type}/{id}/search=….json`; non-search catalog browse and empty `search=` stay refused),
- Media-kind search routes (`/ether/v1/kinds/{kind}/search` with a non-empty query; `/resolve`, `/match`, `/items`, and `/live` stay refused),
- Declared frontend adapter search routes (`/ether/v1/frontend/{key}/…` matching `contributes.frontendAdapters[].searchPaths`, or conventional `/search`, `/search2`, `/search3` subpaths when `searchPaths` is omitted) with a non-empty query (`searchQuery` in the request body is required for routes without a URL query parameter such as GraphQL POST endpoints).

Every other viewer/client path (`/stream/*`, non-search `/catalog/*`, `/meta/*`, `/subtitles/*`, `/ether/open*`, `/ether/metadata/*`, `/ether/subtitles/*`, `/ether/markers*`, `/ether/v1/kinds/*/resolve|match|items|live`, non-search `/ether/v1/frontend/*`, `/ether/view/*`, `/ether/options/*`, `/ether/health`, `/ether/configure`, `/ether/file/*`, `/ether/directory/*`, and hot-path `rank_key`/`cond_match`) stays refused. Remote plugins forward `X-Ether-Viewer-Token` on frontend-adapter search calls (handled automatically by the SDKs) so the host enforces the active adapter route, viewer rate limit, and live grant.

## Bounds, caching & error codes
Safe per-plugin defaults apply with no extra owner settings: 1..20 messages (`system`, `user`, `assistant`, with at least one `user`), 32 KiB total prompt bytes, 32 KiB JSON Schema (external `$ref` URLs are rejected), `maxTokens` default 1024 / max 4096, `temperature` in `[0, 2]`, and 64 KiB response cap.
- Background/action routes: 20 calls/minute per plugin, `timeoutMs` default/max 30 s.
- Interactive search routes (`complete+search`): hard per-request ceiling `timeoutMs` <= 20 s (matching Ether's own descriptive search bound; always catch `timeout`/`deadline` and return non-AI results), per-query host caching (10 min TTL, 256 entries per plugin, normalized query + request fingerprint, concurrent in-flight dedup) so repeated searches do not re-ask the model, and a separate per-viewer rate limit (10 uncached calls/minute per viewer) that never spends the background budget.

Error codes (`err.code` in JS/TS/Python, `HostError.Code` in Go): `not_configured` (HTTP 501 — no language model configured; does not consume rate limit), `forbidden` (hosted) / `permission_denied` (HTTP 403 remote — missing/revoked `ai` or `ai.search` grant, missing `searchQuery`, or disallowed client route), `rate_limited` (HTTP 429), `invalid_input` (hosted) / `invalid` (HTTP 400 remote), `invalid_output` (HTTP 502 — reply was not valid JSON, oversized, or failed `schema`), `timeout` (hosted) / `deadline` (HTTP 504 remote — return non-AI search results), `unavailable` (HTTP 503 — provider call failed, sanitized).

The declarations and implementations below specify arguments, return types, defaults, permission checks, limits, and errors. SDK adapters translate raw hosted calls to portable clients. See [SDKs](/plugins/reference/sdk-typescript) and [Errors](/plugins/reference/troubleshooting).

## Media container probing

Reads container metadata (`{durationSec, container, width, height, sizeBytes}`) for any `PlayableSource` in the same shape `/resolve` returns, reusing Ether's durable `release_probes` cache. Requires `permissions.media: "probe"` (shown on the install sheet as "Probes media container metadata" and revocable live as `media`).

```ts
const probe = ether.media.probe({
  id: "ep-01",
  pattern: "release",
  mime: "video/x-matroska",
  release: { infoHash, fileIndex: 1 },
});
// probe => { durationSec: 2280.4, container: "mkv", width: 1920, height: 1080, sizeBytes: 1234567890 }
```

## Route policy & bounds
`media.probe` is allowed only on jobs (`/ether/job/*`), actions (`/ether/action/*`), Flow actions, tools, event handlers, setup/test routes, feed routes, background kind/Live TV sync, or declared `ether.schedule` routes. Every interactive viewer or client request path (`/resolve`, `/search`, `/catalog/*`, `/stream/*`, `/meta/*`, `/subtitles/*`, `/ether/v1/frontend/*`, `/ether/view/*`, `/ether/options/*`, `/ether/health`, `/ether/configure`, and remote calls carrying `X-Ether-Viewer-Token`) is refused. Each call is bounded at 10 s and per-plugin rate-limited (60 calls/minute). Release probes run strictly cached-only without queuing uncached debrid downloads; URL, folder, secret, and blob permissions still apply per source pattern.

For playback-time verification without calling `media.probe`, set both `durationSec` and `durationToleranceSec` (> 0) on a `PlayableSource` returned by `/resolve`: Ether probes the container header on open (reusing `release_probes`) and rejects mismatches beyond `durationToleranceSec` as wrong content so the next candidate is tried.

## Archive member reads

Hosted and remote clients can keep large data in the host's existing library
blob cache, reading only the metadata or descriptor bytes the plugin itself must parse.
Big media (streams, ROMs, disc images, firmware downloads) never goes through
`cache.read`, `archive.open`, or `archive.read` — Ether streams cached blobs and archive
members directly to clients itself (for example via frontend `{ blob: { libraryKey, ref, memberIndex } }`
descriptors in `internal/plugins/frontend_blob.go` and `frontend.streamURL`); these calls
are strictly for bytes the plugin must parse:

```ts
const limits = await ctx.ether.runtime!.limits();
const readBudget = limits.readBytes ?? 8 * 1024 * 1024; // clamp(memoryBytes / 4, 8 MiB, 512 MiB)
const cached = await ctx.ether.http.fetchToCache!({
  url: "https://datasets.example/platform.zip",
  libraryKey: "pk-community-example-library-games", // this plugin's own library
  name: "platform.zip",
});
const members = await ctx.ether.archive!.list(cached.blob);

// Batch up to 4096 members per call within readBytes:
const xmlMembers = members.filter(m => !m.unsafe && m.name.endsWith(".xml") && m.size > 0);
let batch: Array<{ member: number; offset: number; length: number }> = [];
let batchBytes = 0;
for (const m of xmlMembers) {
  const length = Math.min(m.size, readBudget);
  if (batch.length === 4096 || batchBytes + length > readBudget) {
    const results = await ctx.ether.archive!.read(cached.blob, batch);
    // results: [{ index, member, size, body: Uint8Array }] in request order
    batch = [];
    batchBytes = 0;
  }
  batch.push({ member: m.index, offset: 0, length });
  batchBytes += length;
}
if (batch.length > 0) {
  await ctx.ether.archive!.read(cached.blob, batch);
}

const extracted = await ctx.ether.archive!.extract(cached.blob, xmlMembers[0]!.index);
// {ref: "blob:<sha256>", size, sha1, md5, crc32} streamed directly into the library cache
```

`http.fetchToCache({url, headers?, keepHeadersOnRedirect?, libraryKey, name, timeoutMs?, resume?})` performs a GET, streams
up to the owner download ceiling (8 GiB by default), further bounded by the library cache quota, into the plugin's own library cache, and returns
`{blob, size, crc32, md5, sha1, status}`. SHA-256 is the blob reference.
Digests cover the stored response bytes in one pass. Compare the digest with
trusted catalogue metadata before serving a verified download. Non-2xx responses,
network failures, size overflow and quota failures return errors; they do not
publish a truncated blob. Redirects recheck the live network grant and the
existing SSRF policy. The existing content capability, network host declaration
and library cache quota apply; no new permission is needed. `timeoutMs` defaults
to 10 minutes (also the ceiling on viewer and interactive request paths); in a
job (`/ether/job/*`), schedule, or background context, `timeoutMs` may extend up
to the calling job's remaining deadline. Pass `resume: true` to continue a
partial download with `Range: bytes=<cached>-` when the server supports ranges
and strong `ETag` / `Last-Modified` validators match (restarting cleanly from
byte 0 otherwise); partial blobs obey per-library cache quotas and disk safety
and only become readable cache blobs once complete. The operation is
synchronous; there is no background
prefetch. Cache eviction still applies to returned refs.

The per-call byte ceiling `readBytes` for `cache.read`, `archive.open`, and `archive.read`
scales with the plugin's granted memory: `readBytes = clamp(memoryBytes / 4, 8 MiB, 512 MiB)`
(default 32 MiB plugin memory → 8 MiB per call; declaring `runtime.limits.memoryBytes` of 1 GiB
grants 256 MiB per call). Plugins inspect their live grant via `runtime.limits`
(`ctx.ether.runtime!.limits()`, `BlobHost.RuntimeLimits`, `host.runtime.limits()`, or
`GET /ether/plugin-host/limits`) to size batches without guessing.

`cache.read(blob, {offset, length})` reads `1..readBytes` from a cached blob.
`archive.list(blob)` returns `[{index, name, size, unsafe?, unsafeReason?}]`, reading ZIP, 7z or RAR (4.x/5.x) headers
without loading all compressed bytes. `archive.open(blob, memberIndex, {offset, length})`
returns `1..readBytes` from one **uncompressed** member, while `archive.read(blob, reads)`
reads `1..4096` `{member, offset, length}` ranges in one call whose requested `length`s sum
to at most `readBytes` (returning an error rather than truncating when exceeded) and returns
`[{index, member, size, body}]` in request order (`bodyBase64` on raw JSON wire calls).
Use `archive.open` when reading one member or stepping sequentially through a single large
member across range calls. Use `archive.read` when parsing many small or medium members from
the same cached archive, amortizing cache ownership checks, directory lookup, and host crossings
into a single call. Offsets are nonnegative integers; a read at EOF returns empty bytes and reads
crossing EOF return the available suffix. Every call opens only the calling plugin's cache
namespace and closes every member stream and blob handle before returning.
`archive.extract(blob, memberIndex[, {libraryKey?, name?}])` streams the
uncompressed member directly into the plugin's own library blob cache (defaulting to
the source archive's library namespace) in one pass with no full in-memory buffer,
computing `{ref, size, sha1, md5, crc32}` (`ref` is `"blob:<sha256>"`). It enforces
`archiveMemberBytes` and the target library's cache quota, falls back to
`member-<index>` as the cache entry name when `options.name` is omitted for an unsafe
member name, refuses directories, observes cancellation and
deadlines, and charges governance units per started MiB (`ArchiveExtractUnitsPerMiB`).
The Go `RemoteHostClient` provides `RuntimeLimits`, `FetchToCache`, `CacheRead`, `ArchiveList`,
`ArchiveOpen`, `ArchiveRead`, and `ArchiveExtract` through `BlobHost`; the Python
`RemoteHostClient` and `MockHostClient` expose `runtime.limits()` and `archive.list`,
`archive.open`, `archive.read`, and `archive.extract`.

Archive sizes and member counts use owner global/per-plugin ceilings: defaults
are 8 GiB compressed archive/member, 32 GiB total expansion and 65,535 members.
Member names are limited to 1024 bytes. ZIP supports Store/Deflate and ZIP64;
7z supports Copy, LZMA and LZMA2 (including solid blocks); RAR supports stored
and compressed 4.x/5.x members. Other 7z coder chains are refused, including
BCJ filters and PPMd. Split/multi-volume input, encrypted headers or members,
links and other special files are refused. `archive.list` flags unsafe member
names with `unsafe: true` and `unsafeReason` as informational warnings (never
use stored names as filesystem paths), while `archive.open`, `archive.read`,
`archive.extract`, and frontend blob streaming open any non-directory member by
index. Directories may appear
in listings but cannot be opened. A 1000:1 expansion ceiling applies per ZIP
member and per 7z/RAR compression block. Nothing is extracted to a filesystem.

Metadata and decoder allocations are bounded by `memoryBytes` (32 MiB by
default). ZIP directories also retain the 64 MiB host ceiling. A large dictionary
or directory can be refused even when the member fits the byte grant. 7z uses
at most half the memory grant for its dictionary; RAR reserves one eighth per
decoder buffer, including PPMd and filters. Compressed input bytes read, including
metadata and decoder read-ahead, are cumulatively bounded by `fetchBytes` per
call. Expanded solid blocks and the whole declared expansion are bounded by
`archiveExpandedBytes`. Calls observe the runtime deadline and cancellation.

A range is a bound on **returned bytes**, not decompression work. Deflate reads
start at the member beginning. Solid 7z/RAR ranges decode dependencies from the
block beginning, then discard bytes through the requested offset. Calls are
stateless: sequential calls also restart decoding. RAR can additionally consume
earlier solid blocks in archive order. Prefer large sequential
chunks and avoid repeated random reads; persist verification digests in KV.
Range reads do not independently verify the full member CRC; use trusted digests
when integrity matters. Local owner-granted paths are not archive inputs: first
use a plugin-owned cached blob. Gzip files are unsupported here.
An HTTP `Content-Encoding: gzip` response may be transparently decoded by the
HTTP client; its digests then describe the decoded bytes. A `.gz` file is not
automatically decompressed by this archive service.

Direct `http.fetch` still limits the raw response to 10 MiB, with its JSON result
allowance including encoding expansion. Hosted WASM host-result envelopes also scale
automatically with the plugin's `readBytes` grant (including base64 and JSON framing
overhead, with a 4 MiB baseline floor), while hosted QuickJS binary reads transfer
decoded bytes directly into guest `ArrayBuffer`s. Big media never goes through these
read calls — Ether streams blobs and archive members itself (`internal/plugins/frontend_blob.go`).

## Source: docs/plugin-debrid.md

# Native debrid providers

A hosted source plugin may declare `debrid_provider` and
`ether.contributes.source.class: "debrid"`. Its account belongs in secret settings,
read with `ether.secret.get`. It registers automatically with the native debrid
pipeline while enabled; disabling or removing the plugin unregisters it.

The host sends JSON POST requests to these routes:

| Route under `/ether/debrid/` | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check` | `{hashes: string[]}` | `{cached: Record<string, boolean>}` |
| `find` | `{infoHash}` | `{torrentId}` |
| `acquire` | `{infoHash, magnet, torrentId, cachedOnly}` | `{torrentId, ready, added, files: [{id, path, size, link?}]}` |
| `link` | `{torrentId, fileId, path, link, magnet, infoHash, size}` | `{url, size, expires?}` |
| `remove` | `{torrentId}` | `{}` |
| `account` | `{}` | `{user, premium, expires?}` |

Times are RFC3339. File sizes are bytes. `added` must be true only when this
request created the provider torrent. The host selects the movie or episode
from `files`; it never sends executable selection callbacks to a plugin.
Unready acquisitions become cache misses. Cleanup only applies to newly added
torrents when the caller's removal policy permits it. A cached-only service may
return HTTP 501 for `find` and `remove`.

HTTP 401/403 means invalid credentials, 404/410 gone, 409 not cached, 429 rate
limited, and 501 unsupported. Other failures use a generic provider error.
Plugin links must be public HTTP(S) URLs; both link validation and every network
dial/redirect use the guarded transport. Native retry, cache, limiter and file
selection behavior applies. Plugin providers currently run after configured
built-in providers at priority 1000; source-card display order does not change
that priority.

Provide `/ether/health` with `status: "attention"` and a useful `reason` when
credentials are absent. `/ether/test` should verify the account and return
`{ok, message}` without exposing credentials or signed URLs. Offline installation
checks cannot establish that a paid account works; test it after setup.

## Cache hints

A source or integration plugin that knows which torrents a debrid service
already holds may declare `debrid_cache_hints`. It needs no contribution block
and no debrid account of its own. Ether calls `POST /ether/debrid/hints` only
when source preparation checks the shortlist for one of two starts: Vela's
playback request and Silo's playback start, including one that names a
version (not a queued next item). Nothing else asks: not Jellyfin or Emby
clients (some send `IsPlayback` true for queue prefetches, so a `PlaybackInfo`
does not prove a Play), not Plex clients, a lazy stream fetch or file probe,
WebDAV, Stremio or Xtream, a detail page, a console search, a warm-up or
prefetch, a download, the next episode or a queue advance, a version switch
during playback, failover to another release or a background check. It is not
called either when the lead torrent is already known cached, in memory or by
an account's remembered answer.

```json
{"candidates": [
  {"infoHash": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567", "private": false, "providerKinds": ["realdebrid", "torbox"]},
  {"infoHash": "89abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef", "private": true, "providerKinds": ["realdebrid"]}
]}
```

The request lists at most the 12 torrents preparation looks at. For each hash,
`providerKinds` names the enabled debrid services (`realdebrid`, `torbox`,
`alldebrid`, `premiumize`, `debridlink`, `offcloud`, or `plugin:<id>` for a
plugin provider) with an account that has no answer of its own for that hash,
neither a recent check nor an answer the account remembers from an add;
hashes every service has answered are left out. `private` is true when any
copy of the torrent comes from a private tracker. A plugin that sends hashes to
an outside service decides what it sends there: leave private hashes out unless
the owner opted in.

```json
{"cached": {"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567": ["realdebrid"]}}
```

List only the hashes and kinds known to be cached. Ether keeps only the pairs it
asked about and treats them like an add-on's cached marker: a hint in memory for
30 minutes that never replaces an account's own answer, and an account with a
hint is tried before the others when the torrent is added. A miss, an error or a
missing hash writes nothing. One 500 ms deadline, started before Ether reads
what it knows, covers every hint plugin together; a plugin whose instances are
all busy is skipped, and an answer after the deadline is ignored. A timeout, on
that deadline or on the route's own, does not count against the plugin's health.
Answer from what the plugin already knows or can learn at once, and never wait
for a rate limiter on this route.


## Source: docs/plugin-kinds.md

# Plugin content kinds

A content plugin adds a whole **library** to Ether — audiobooks,
comics, music, books, photos, field recordings, anything flat or
hierarchical — with no core changes. The owner meets each kind you
declare as a library beside Movies and TV Shows, in the console and
in every client app you publish it to.

This page is the contract. The worked example is
[`sdk/examples/kind-library`](../sdk/examples/kind-library); the
Studio "A new library" template generates the same skeleton from a
description.

## Declare a kind

In the manifest's `ether` block: `kind: "content"`, at least one of
the `catalog_provider` / `kind_resolver` capabilities (plus optional
`matcher` and `frontend_adapter`), and one entry per kind in
`contributes.mediaKinds`:

```jsonc
{
  "key": "recordings",              // ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$, unique in the plugin
  "label": "Field recordings",
  "media": "music",                 // optional: video|music|audiobook|book|podcast|photo
  "library": {
    "name": "Field recordings",     // default name; the owner can rename
    "card": "landscape",            // optional: poster (default) | landscape | square
    "dateDisplay": "date",          // optional: year (default) | date (full YYYY-MM-DD)
    "experience": "listen",         // optional: watch | listen | read | gallery | live, or another id (default by media class)
    "tabs": [                       // optional (<= 50); defaults to Recommended + Library
      { "key": "recommended", "label": "Recommended", "kind": "recommended" },
      { "key": "library", "label": "Library", "kind": "library" },
      { "key": "albums", "label": "Albums", "kind": "library", "level": "album" }
    ]
  },
  "levels": [                       // 1–5 levels, first is the root
    { "key": "collection", "label": "Collection", "role": "artist" },
    { "key": "album", "label": "Album", "role": "album", "container": true },
    { "key": "track", "label": "Track", "role": "track", "playable": true }
  ],
  "fields": [                       // validated per item; indexed ones can facet
    { "key": "genre", "type": "string", "label": "Genre", "indexed": true },
    { "key": "durationSec", "type": "duration", "label": "Duration", "indexed": true }
  ],
  "present": { /* see "Publishing" */ },
  "browse": {
    "sorts": ["title", "index"],
    "facets": ["genre", "durationSec"],
    "search": true,
    "liveSearch": true,
    "expand": { "facets": ["genre"], "levels": ["artist", "album"], "ttlHours": 168 } // optional on-demand slice & container expansion
  },
  "sync": { "mode": "pull", "refresh": "1h" },
  "cache": { "maxBytes": 2147483648 },        // optional; per-library blob cache
  "match": { "thresholdDefault": 0.8 }        // optional
}
```

Rules that will bite if ignored: at least one level must be
`playable`; facet fields must be `indexed` (except `people`, which is
always indexed); `enum` fields declare a closed `enum` list, while
`strings` fields may declare an optional `values` vocabulary shown in the
rules editor even before any item carries them; field keys may not reuse
envelope names (`id`, `title`, …); declarations are **additive across
versions** — removing or retyping a field/level is refused at upgrade
unless the owner agrees to replace the library's contents.

### Library presentation, sub-tabs, sorts and facets in Vela

`library` and `browse` shape how Vela renders the library without per-plugin client logic:

- `media` and `levels[].role`: optional semantic hints (`media`: `"video"`, `"music"`, `"audiobook"`, `"book"`, `"podcast"`, or `"photo"`; `role`: `"item"`, `"artist"`, `"album"`, `"track"`, `"series"`, `"book"`, `"audiobook"`, `"part"`, `"show"`, `"episode"`, or `"collection"`). A level may also declare `parent` (to branch from an earlier level rather than the previous one) and its own `media` class (for example a `video` concert branch under a `music` artist). For containers with stored children, `media.childCounts` carries direct-child counts keyed by child role (or level key when role-less) from the indexed per-level tally on both list and detail responses, and `media.childCount` is the direct-child total (the sum over `media.childCounts`, not the recursive leaf count). On a branching container's detail response (`GET /vela/v0/titles/{id}`), `seasons` lists only the primary child level (the first child level matching the container's media class, else the first declared child level); other child branches are listed via `GET /vela/v0/titles/{id}/children?role=<role>`. Music kinds (`media: "music"`) and `"track"`-role items are excluded from Continue Watching and skip saving mid-track resume offsets while still recording playback timestamps and completions so history shelves work. Other media classes automatically localize the Continue shelf title per request locale (`Continue Watching` for video/photo, `Continue Reading` for book, `Continue Listening` for audiobook/podcast).
- `library.icon`: optional package-relative SVG or PNG. Ether fetches it alongside the manifest on URL install and serves it at `/ether/api/plugins/<id>/icon?kind=<key>`. The console uses it for the catalogue and library, with `ether.icon` and then the Stremio `logo` as fallbacks.
- `library.card`: `"poster"` (2:3, default), `"landscape"` (16:9; Ether serves the item's `thumb`, else `backdrop`, as `artwork[]` kind `"thumb"`, falling back to `poster`), or `"square"` (1:1).
- `library.dateDisplay`: `"year"` (default) or `"date"`. When set to `"date"`, Vela receives `"dateDisplay": "date"` on the library (and on projected items alongside canonical `"airDate": "YYYY-MM-DD"`), and both Vela and the owner console display full `YYYY-MM-DD` dates from `item.released` instead of year-only labels. Useful for dated broadcasts, tournament VODs, or daily recordings.
- `library.experience`: how apps present the whole library, as an experience id. Ether's ids are `"watch"` (films and TV: the app's ordinary library pages and tabs), `"listen"` (a listening app — in Vela a library sidebar, a persistent now-playing bar, a queue and full-screen Now Playing, in place of the tab strip), `"read"` (books and comics), `"gallery"` (photos and home videos) and `"live"` (a guide, multiview, sports). The set is open: any id matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$` is accepted, and an app that does not know an id presents the library as `watch`. It defaults by the kind's media class: `listen` for `music`, `audiobook` and `podcast`; `read` for `book`; `gallery` for `photo`; `watch` for everything else — so a music kind opts out with `"watch"` and a sports kind opts into `"live"`. Vela receives it as `experience` at the top level of every `/vela/v0/libraries` entry (always sent), and `features.libraryExperiences.experiences` lists Ether's ids. It is library-level only and unrelated to a tab's `layout` (`grid`/`list`/`timeline`). In the listen experience Vela builds its pages from the same data as any library: the library's rows (a `continue` row reads "Continue listening"), item roles, `media.credits` (author, narrator, host), episode dates and durations, played state and resume, and chapters.
- `library.tabs`: up to 50 entries of `{key, label, kind, level?, facet?, order?, card?, layout?, search?, searchPlaceholder?, sort?, direction?, filters?}` where `kind` is `"recommended"`, `"library"`, `"collections"`, `"people"`, `"view"`, or `"live"`. Keys match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$` and are unique within the library; labels support `$t:` keys and follow copy rules (≤40 characters). Omitting `tabs` defaults to `Recommended` (`recommended`) and `Library` (`library`). `library`, `view`, `collections`, and `people` tabs may set optional `level` (naming a declared `levels[].key`) to scope browsing, facets, facet collections, and people lists to a non-root hierarchy level (for example an `Albums` or `Tracks` tab on an `artist -> album -> track` kind). Vela exposes `level` on each tab and accepts `?level=<key>` on `/items` and `/facets/{field}` (or inherits the tab's `level` from `?tab=<key>`); Plex `?type=8/9/10` and Jellyfin `IncludeItemTypes=MusicArtist/MusicAlbum/Audio` resolve to matching declared levels on the indexed SQL path.
  - **`"collections"` tabs**: may set `facet` (one of `browse.facets`), `order` (`"count"` default, or `"name"` for case-insensitive alphabetical ordering), `search` (`true` by default; set `false` to hide in-tab search), `searchPlaceholder` (optional localizable `$t:` or literal copy, ≤60 characters, when `search` is enabled), `sort` (one of `browse.sorts` or `"lastViewed"`), and `direction` (`"asc"` or `"desc"`, defaulting to `released` `desc` when `released` is declared). `GET /vela/v0/libraries/{id}/collections?tab=<tabKey>&query=<text>` pages those facet buckets (optionally filtered by case- and diacritic-insensitive word prefix on `query`, 1–100 characters after trimming) with the newest item's artwork, and opening one navigates to `/vela/v0/libraries/{id}/items?facet.<field>=<valueId>&sort=&direction=` (or `?collectionId=facet:<field>:<valueId>`).
  - **`"people"` tabs**: require `facet` referencing a declared `browse.facets` entry whose field has `type: "people"`, and accept `order` (`"name"` case-insensitive alphabetical by default, or `"count"`), `search` (`true` by default), and `searchPlaceholder` (optional localizable `$t:` or literal copy, ≤60 characters, when `search` is enabled). `sort` and `direction` are not used on `"people"` tabs. `GET /vela/v0/libraries/{id}/collections?tab=<tabKey>&query=<text>` pages the distinct root-level people in that field (with the same `query` word-prefix filter when `search` is enabled) as `{"id":"person:<personId>","kind":"person","person":{"id":"<personId>","name":"…","photo":…},"itemCount":N,"receiptToken":""}`, with portraits resolved in one batch per page; `<personId>` opens `GET /vela/v0/people/{id}` and `/vela/v0/people/{id}/titles`.
  - **`"view"` tabs (Smart Views)**: define filtered, sorted sub-views inside the library — including per-viewer History, Watchlist, Favorites, Unwatched, or field-filtered tabs. Accepts optional `layout` (`"grid"` default, `"list"`, or `"timeline"`), `sort` (one of `browse.sorts` or `"lastViewed"`), `direction` (`"asc"` or `"desc"`, defaulting to `"desc"` for `"lastViewed"`), `search` (`true` by default), `searchPlaceholder` (≤60 characters when `search` is enabled), and `filters` (`{match?: "all"|"any", rules: [...], exclude?: [...]}`). Filter rules may target declared indexed fields (`"browse:<field>"`, `"year"`, `"rating"`, or mapped indexed facts) and per-viewer state (`{"field":"viewer","op":"is","value":{...}}` supporting `history`, `watched`, `unwatched`, `inProgress`, `favorite`, `watchlist`, `lastViewedAfter`, and `lastViewedBefore`, evaluated strictly for the requesting viewer). Vela reads items via `GET /vela/v0/libraries/{id}/items?tab=<tabKey>` and receives `title.watch.lastViewedAt` (RFC3339 UTC) on viewed items.
  - **`"live"` tabs**: surface ephemeral currently-live streams inside the library without registering Live TV channels or requiring Live TV setup. Accepts optional `card` (`"landscape"` default, `"poster"`, or `"square"`), `search` (`true` by default), and `searchPlaceholder` (≤60 characters when `search` is enabled); `facet`, `order`, `sort`, and `direction` are not used. Vela lists items via `GET /vela/v0/libraries/{id}/live?tab=&query=&filter=&cursor=&limit=` and starts playback via `POST /vela/v0/libraries/{id}/live/play` (returning a standard Vela `PlaybackPlan` and session). Thumbnails are proxied and signed by Ether — upstream URLs never reach clients.
  - For example, a documentary & broadcasts library can combine dated items (`dateDisplay: "date"`), a searchable `"live"` tab, tournament collections, and a per-viewer `"view"` History tab:
    ```json
    "library": {
      "name": "Documentaries",
      "card": "landscape",
      "dateDisplay": "date",
      "tabs": [
        { "key": "live", "label": "Live", "kind": "live", "card": "landscape", "searchPlaceholder": "Search live streams" },
        { "key": "recommended", "label": "Recommended", "kind": "recommended" },
        { "key": "library", "label": "Library", "kind": "library" },
        { "key": "topics", "label": "Topics", "kind": "collections", "facet": "topic", "order": "name", "searchPlaceholder": "Search topics" },
        {
          "key": "history",
          "label": "History",
          "kind": "view",
          "layout": "timeline",
          "sort": "lastViewed",
          "direction": "desc",
          "searchPlaceholder": "Search watch history",
          "filters": {
            "match": "all",
            "rules": [
              { "field": "viewer", "op": "is", "value": { "history": true } }
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    }
    ```
- `browse.sorts` and `browse.facets`: surfaced directly on `GET /vela/v0/libraries` under `browse.sorts` and `browse.filters.facets` (with `"lastViewed"` always available for recently watched ordering). Facet values are paged at `GET /vela/v0/libraries/{id}/facets/{field}` (`int`, `date`, and `duration` fields are served as discrete buckets — years for `date`, duration ranges for `duration`, and distinct integers up to 50 or ranges above 50) and filtered with repeatable `facet.<field>=<bucketId>` on `GET /vela/v0/libraries/{id}/items` alongside in-library `query=`.
- Recommended rows (`GET /vela/v0/libraries/{id}/rows`):
  - Accepts optional `?tab=<tabKey>` to query a specific `"recommended"` tab's shelves. An unknown `tab` id answers `404` (`not_found`), and a tab whose `kind` is not `"recommended"` answers `400` (`unsupported_library_query`).
  - When `library.shelves` is omitted, Ether builds auto-generated shelves (up to 8 by default, 20 items each) from your stored items — Continue watching, Newest, Recently added, Top rated (when `rating` is a declared sort), and daily-rotating values from your declared facets.
  - To define curated default Recommended shelves directly in the manifest, declare `library.shelves` (up to 40 entries). When `library.shelves` is non-empty, Ether prepends Continue watching whenever the viewer has in-progress items, then evaluates each declared shelf in order (up to 20 items each, skipping empty shelves) without clamping to the auto-generated 8-row default. Each shelf receives the stable row ID `plugin:<viewID>:shelf:<key>`, so the library's Recommended row editor can reorder, hide, pin, or set `MaxRows` (owner overrides always win). `GET /vela/v0/libraries/{id}/rows` supports cursor pagination (`limit` and `cursor` query parameters, returning `items`, `continuation`: `"more" | "exhausted"`, and `nextCursor`) so clients can page through 30+ shelves:
    ```json
    "shelves": [
      { "key": "jump-back-in", "label": "Jump back in", "level": "album", "sort": "lastViewed", "direction": "desc", "purpose": "recentContexts", "filters": [{ "field": "viewer", "value": { "history": true } }] },
      { "key": "recently-played", "label": "Recently played", "level": "track", "sort": "lastViewed", "layout": "tracks" },
      { "key": "latest-episodes", "label": "Latest episodes", "sort": "released", "direction": "desc" },
      { "key": "science-nature", "label": "Science and nature", "facet": "topic", "values": ["Science", "Nature"] },
      { "key": "longform-history", "label": "$t:shelf_longform_history", "sort": "rating", "direction": "desc", "filters": { "topic": ["History"], "format": ["Feature", "Miniseries"] } }
    ]
    ```
    Each shelf accepts:
    - `key` (required): unique in the library, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$`.
    - `label` (required): literal or `$t:<key>`, at most 60 characters.
    - `level` (optional): declared `levels[].key` to query instead of the root level.
    - `sort` (optional, default `"released"`): one of `title`, `added`, `released`, `year`, `rating`, `index`, `lastViewed`.
    - `direction` (optional, default `"desc"`): `"desc"` or `"asc"`.
    - Optional filtering: either `facet` plus `value` or `values` (OR), or `filters` as either a legacy facet map (`{ "<facet>": ["..."] }`, AND across facets, OR within each facet), a `TabFilter` object (`{ match?, rules, exclude? }`), a single rule object, or a list of rules (`[{ "field": "viewer", "value": { "history": true } }]`; omitted `"op"` on `"viewer"` rules defaults to `"is"`). Every referenced field must be a declared indexed field (or `people` field, or envelope facet `year`/`released`/`rating`, or `"viewer"`). Viewer history filters and `lastViewed` ordering roll descendant playback up to ancestor containers (so playing a track surfaces its album on an `album`-level `lastViewed` shelf without ever leaking unviewed items).
