Hosted and remote clients can keep large data in the host's existing library
blob cache, reading only the metadata or descriptor bytes the plugin itself must parse.
Big media (video/audio streams, ROMs, disc images, firmware downloads) never goes through
`cache.read`, `archive.open`, or `archive.read` — Ether streams cached blobs and archive
members directly to clients itself (for example via frontend `{ blob: { libraryKey, ref, memberIndex } }`
descriptors in `internal/plugins/frontend_blob.go`, `frontend.streamURL`, and playable container sources):

```ts
const limits = await ctx.ether.runtime!.limits();
const readBudget = limits.readBytes ?? 8 * 1024 * 1024; // clamp(memoryBytes / 4, 8 MiB, 512 MiB)
const cached = await ctx.ether.http.fetchToCache!({
  url: "https://datasets.example/platform.zip",
  libraryKey: "pk-community-example-library-games", // this plugin's own library
  name: "platform.zip",
});
const members = await ctx.ether.archive!.list(cached.blob);

// Batch up to 4096 small/medium members per call within readBytes:
const xmlMembers = members.filter(m => !m.unsafe && m.name.endsWith(".xml") && m.size > 0);
let batch: Array<{ member: number; offset: number; length: number }> = [];
let batchBytes = 0;
for (const m of xmlMembers) {
  const length = Math.min(m.size, readBudget);
  if (batch.length === 4096 || batchBytes + length > readBudget) {
    const results = await ctx.ether.archive!.read(cached.blob, batch);
    // results: [{ index, member, size, body: Uint8Array }] in request order
    batch = [];
    batchBytes = 0;
  }
  batch.push({ member: m.index, offset: 0, length });
  batchBytes += length;
}
if (batch.length > 0) {
  await ctx.ether.archive!.read(cached.blob, batch);
}

const extracted = await ctx.ether.archive!.extract(cached.blob, xmlMembers[0]!.index);
// {ref: "blob:<sha256>", size, sha1, md5, crc32} streamed directly into the library cache
```

`http.fetchToCache({url, headers?, keepHeadersOnRedirect?, libraryKey, name, timeoutMs?, resume?, connections?})` performs a GET, streams
up to the owner download ceiling (8 GiB by default), subject to the media budget and any library limit, into the plugin's library namespace, and returns
`{blob, size, crc32, md5, sha1, status}`. SHA-256 is the blob reference.
Digests cover the stored response bytes in one pass. Compare the digest with
trusted catalogue metadata before serving a verified download. Non-2xx responses,
network failures, size overflow and quota failures return errors; they do not
publish a truncated blob. Redirects recheck the live network grant and the
existing SSRF policy, and follow the same redirect credential policy as
`http.fetch` (keep credentials/headers on same origin, strict same-site
subdomains, or explicit `keepHeadersOnRedirect` hosts within granted network
permissions; never across HTTPS→HTTP downgrades). The existing content capability, network host declaration
and library cache quota apply; no new permission is needed. `timeoutMs` defaults
to 10 minutes (also the ceiling on viewer and interactive request paths); in a
job (`/ether/job/*`), schedule, or background context, `timeoutMs` may extend up
to the calling job's remaining deadline. Pass `resume: true` to continue an
incomplete partial blob with `Range: bytes=<cached>-` when the server supports
ranges and strong `ETag` / `Last-Modified` validators match (restarting cleanly
from byte 0 when validators mismatch or the server ignores ranges); partial
blobs obey per-library cache quotas, the media pool budget, and the disk free-space
floor, and become readable via `cache.open` / `cache.read` / `archive.*` only
when complete. Jobs, schedules, and background calls can request `connections`
from 1 to 6 (default 1), sharing the host's limit of 6 per origin. When the
server advertises byte ranges, a known length, and a strong validator,
Ether fetches ranges in parallel and hashes the assembled file. Ranges served
from a different URL need the same strong ETag and total length as the probe. With
`resume: true`, retries continue each range's saved progress.
Incompatible range responses fall back to a single download. The operation
runs synchronously within the calling plugin invocation. Cache eviction still applies to returned refs.

The per-call byte ceiling `readBytes` for `cache.read`, `archive.open`, and `archive.read`
scales with the plugin's granted memory: `readBytes = clamp(memoryBytes / 4, 8 MiB, 512 MiB)`
(default 32 MiB plugin memory → 8 MiB per call; declaring `runtime.limits.memoryBytes` of 1 GiB
grants 256 MiB per call). Plugins read their live grant via `runtime.limits`
(`ctx.ether.runtime!.limits()` in TypeScript, `BlobHost.RuntimeLimits(ctx)` in Go,
`host.runtime.limits()` in Python, or `GET /ether/plugin-host/limits`) so batch sizes never rely
on hardcoded guesses.

`cache.read(blob, {offset, length})` reads `1..readBytes` from a cached blob.
`archive.list(blob)` returns `[{index, name, size, unsafe?, unsafeReason?}]`, reading ZIP, 7z or RAR (4.x/5.x) headers
without loading all compressed bytes. `archive.open(blob, memberIndex, {offset, length})`
returns `1..readBytes` from one **uncompressed** member, while `archive.read(blob, reads)`
reads `1..4096` `{member, offset, length}` ranges in one call whose requested `length`s sum
to at most `readBytes` (returning an error rather than truncating when exceeded) and returns
`[{index, member, size, body}]` in request order (`bodyBase64` on raw JSON wire calls).
Use `archive.open` when reading a single member or stepping sequentially through one large
file across range calls. Use `archive.read` when parsing many small or medium members from the
same cached archive (such as thousands of XML, DAT, or CUE descriptors), amortizing cache
ownership checks, directory lookup, and host crossings into one call.
Offsets are nonnegative integers; a read at EOF returns empty bytes and reads crossing EOF
return the available suffix. Every call opens only the calling plugin's cache namespace and
closes every member stream and blob handle before returning.
`archive.extract(blob, memberIndex[, {libraryKey?, name?}])` streams the
uncompressed member directly into the plugin's own library blob cache (defaulting to
the source archive's library namespace) in one pass with no full in-memory buffer,
computing `{ref, size, sha1, md5, crc32}` (`ref` is `"blob:<sha256>"`). It enforces
`archiveMemberBytes` and the target library's cache quota, falls back to
`member-<index>` as the cache entry name when `options.name` is omitted for an unsafe
member name, refuses directories, observes cancellation and
deadlines, and charges governance units per started MiB (`ArchiveExtractUnitsPerMiB`).
The Go `RemoteHostClient` provides `RuntimeLimits`, `FetchToCache`, `CacheRead`, `CacheRasterize`, `ArchiveList`,
`ArchiveOpen`, `ArchiveRead`, and `ArchiveExtract` through `BlobHost`; the Python
`RemoteHostClient` and `MockHostClient` expose `runtime.limits()` and `archive.list`,
`archive.open`, `archive.read`, and `archive.extract`.

`cache.rasterize(libraryKey, name, sourceBlob[, {width?, height?, format?}])` rasterises an
SVG already in the plugin's own library cache into a new cached bitmap blob, for clients
that only draw bitmaps. It returns `{blob, contentType, width, height, size}`; serve the
result as a blob response like any other cached image. A zero `width` or `height` keeps
the SVG aspect ratio and `format` is `"png"` (default) or `"jpeg"`. The host bounds the
source document (512 KiB) and each output dimension (2048), applies the same SVG safety
rules Ether uses for logos (no external resources, scripts, or unsafe constructs), and
returns an error for documents it refuses. Rendered variants are cached by source content
and size, and the stored blob is content-addressed, so repeat calls return the same
reference. The existing content capability and library cache quota apply; no new
permission is needed.

Archive sizes and member counts use owner global/per-plugin ceilings: defaults
are 8 GiB compressed archive/member, 32 GiB total expansion and 65,535 members.
Unsafe member names remain in listings with `unsafe: true` and `unsafeReason`
as informational warnings so callers never use stored names as filesystem paths.
Empty names, names over 1024 bytes, NUL, backslashes, absolute paths (including
drive-rooted paths), and traversal or noncanonical path segments are flagged.
Because `archive.open`, `archive.read`, `archive.extract`, and frontend blob
streaming address members by index and never write stored names to disk, any
non-directory member (including flagged names such as Windows-style backslash
paths) can be read and extracted by index.
These flags are retained in the cached directory. ZIP supports Store/Deflate and ZIP64;
7z supports Copy, LZMA and LZMA2 (including solid blocks); RAR supports stored
and compressed 4.x/5.x members. Other 7z coder chains are refused, including
BCJ filters and PPMd. Split/multi-volume input, encrypted headers or members,
links and other special files are refused. Directories may appear
in listings but cannot be opened. A 1000:1 expansion ceiling applies per ZIP
member and per 7z/RAR compression block. Nothing is extracted to a filesystem.

Metadata and decoder allocations are bounded by `memoryBytes` (32 MiB by
default). ZIP directories also retain the 64 MiB host ceiling. A large dictionary
or directory can be refused even when the member fits the byte grant. 7z uses
at most half the memory grant for its dictionary; RAR reserves one eighth per
decoder buffer, including PPMd and filters. Compressed input bytes read, including
metadata and decoder read-ahead, are cumulatively bounded by `fetchBytes` per
call. Expanded solid blocks and the whole declared expansion are bounded by
`archiveExpandedBytes`. Calls observe the runtime deadline and cancellation.

A range is a bound on **returned bytes**, not decompression work. Deflate reads
start at the member beginning. Solid 7z/RAR ranges decode dependencies from the
block beginning, then discard bytes through the requested offset. Calls are
stateless: sequential calls also restart decoding. RAR can additionally consume
earlier solid blocks in archive order. Prefer large sequential
chunks and avoid repeated random reads; persist verification digests in KV.
Range reads do not independently verify the full member CRC; use trusted digests
when integrity matters. Local owner-granted paths are not archive inputs: first
use a plugin-owned cached blob. Gzip files are unsupported here.
An HTTP `Content-Encoding: gzip` response may be transparently decoded by the
HTTP client; its digests then describe the decoded bytes. A `.gz` file is not
automatically decompressed by this archive service.

Direct `http.fetch` still limits the raw response to 10 MiB, with its JSON result
allowance including encoding expansion. Hosted WASM host-result envelopes also scale
automatically with the plugin's `readBytes` grant (including base64 and JSON framing
overhead, with a 4 MiB baseline floor), while hosted QuickJS binary reads (`cache.read`,
`archive.open`, `archive.read`) transfer decoded bytes directly into guest `ArrayBuffer`s.
Remember that big media never goes through these read calls — Ether streams blobs and
archive members directly to clients itself (`internal/plugins/frontend_blob.go`); reserve
`cache.read`, `archive.open`, and `archive.read` for bytes the plugin must parse.

### Owner-started multi-call work and resource requests

A page action or scheduled call returning `{job: "build-catalogue"}` starts a background job (up to two owner/scheduled jobs per plugin, separate from playback preparation jobs).
The job returns `continueInMs`, an opaque JSON `continuation`, and a `progress`
string to continue; Ether forwards the token in the next POST body. `done: true`
finishes, `failed: "reason"` fails, and an absent `continueInMs` finishes too.
Jobs use the owner's time ceiling (12h by default), a 1,000,000-call sanity bound,
a minimum 100ms pause, OS background CPU/IO priority, and cooperative pauses
between calls and host operations during playback, Live TV or high host load.
They are cancellable with visible progress. Persist checkpoints in KV for
recovery on a later owner action after restart; Ether does not resume eagerly.

`ether.runtime.limits` requests memory, time, compute, instance pool size, download,
archive and catalogue-item resources within owner-controlled global/per-plugin ceilings.
Defaults: 2 GiB memory ceiling (up to 4 GiB; omitted heap request stays 32 MiB),
12h, effectively unlimited background work units, 2 hosted WASM instances (`poolSize`,
requestable up to the owner ceiling, default ceiling 4 and raisable up to 16; with
`poolSize >= 3` at least one instance is reserved exclusively for playback resolves
and background jobs hold at most `poolSize - 2`; with `poolSize == 2` background jobs
and frontend adapters share at most one instance so playback resolves and health
checks keep one free; queued resolves also take priority and start their execution
deadline once an instance is acquired), 8 GiB download/member,
32 GiB total expansion, 65,535 archive members, and 2,000,000 stored catalogue items
(`maxItems`, with no upper cap when raised by the owner). Remote plugins can
also request data and `maxItems` limits. The library cache quota further bounds
downloads. The owner
sees requested versus granted values before install and in the drawer, and can
raise or lower ceilings under Plugins → Settings or for one plugin. Saving
stops affected jobs so the new ceilings apply immediately.

Viewer search and playback calls derive their unit budget directly from each
route's deadline (`10,000 units/s`): `/stream/*` and `/ether/open*` get 3 s
(30,000 units). `/subtitles/*`, `/ether/subtitles/*`, and kind `/live/resolve`
and `/match` get 5 s (50,000 units). Kind `/resolve` gets 12 s (120,000 units).
`/catalog/*`, `/meta/*`, `/ether/metadata/*`, `/ether/markers*`, and kind `/search`,
`/live`, and `/items/*` get 10 s (100,000 units). `ether.runtime.limits()` reports
the effective limits for the current call.
Background kind catalogue sync (`/browse`, `/changes`, and `/expand`), administrative setup,
actions, tools, events and jobs use owner grants. Health/configuration/view/options/test
keep short protocol deadlines. See `sdk/AGENTS.md` and the SDK README for exact
per-route limits and how owners raise ceilings.

### Pending resolve and match replies

A `/resolve` reply may include both `sources` and `pending: true`. Ether tries
the sources first. If every attempted option is an uncached torrent blocked by
the owner's cache policy or the source's `release.cachedOnly` flag, Ether starts the
optional preparation job and returns `preparing` with the supplied retry hint.
If a torrent can be queued, normal debrid queueing applies. The next Play can
pick up the prepared source through `/resolve`.

Both routes can return `{pending:true,retryInMs:1000,job:"/ether/job/prepare"}`.
`job` is optional. Ether clamps retry delays to 250–5000 ms, retries for up to
25 seconds total per Play, and caps each invocation at 12 seconds for `/resolve`
and five seconds for `/match`.
Pending is neutral for health. When the 25-second budget expires while the reply is still `pending`,
Ether returns `503` with `code: "preparing"` and `Retry-After` set from the last
`retryInMs` (defaulting to `5` seconds) across `kind-media`, Vela,
Jellyfin/MediaBrowser, and Plex API routes, and never saves a negative resolution.
Resolver preparation jobs have their own four-slot pool per plugin (separate from
the two-slot owner/scheduled pool); if all four resolver slots are running, Ether
returns `503` with `code: "jobs_busy"`, `Retry-After`, and the refusal message,
and records the refused job on the plugin Jobs view. A real empty `sources: []`
answer stays `409` `no_source`. A job receives the original request body (including `partIndex` when
resolving a multi-part item and `source` when opening a source-scoped stream ticket), uses promoted deadlines and continuation replies,
and is deduplicated per plugin/kind/item (and `partIndex` / `source`). Job completion wakes
the next resolve.

For remote verification call `ether.http.hash({url,algo:"sha256",expectSize,headers,keepHeadersOnRedirect})`.
A miss returns pending while a bounded host worker streams digests without
storing bytes; the next resolve reads the cached result. Optional `headers`
reject hop-by-hop and framing headers, expand `{secret:<name>}` placeholders via
`permissions.secrets` just like playable sources, follow redirects only under
Ether's redirect credential policy (same origin, strict same-site subdomains, or
explicit `keepHeadersOnRedirect` hosts within granted network permissions; never
across HTTPS→HTTP downgrades), and are never logged or persisted in the hash cache.
Plugins that derive temporary session credentials can store them sealed with
`ether.secret.set(name, value, ttlSec?)` (and clear them with `ether.secret.delete(name)`)
under a declared non-owner name in `permissions.secrets`, then reference them as
`{secret:<name>}` in source headers and `http.hash`. See the worked example
and exact timeout, cache, cancellation and byte limits in [the authoring recipe](../sdk/AGENTS.md#slow-resolution-and-remote-verification).


## Sync viewer watch state

Declare `ether.permissions.viewers.write_watch_state: "granted_viewers"` and
have the owner grant the viewers your plugin may update. Send the selected
viewer's ID, the item ID and a watched boolean. The host accepts a playable
item reference owned by your plugin (`pk:<pluginId>:<kind>:<externalId>`) or a
catalogue movie or episode ID returned by the host catalogue. Provider IDs
accepted by `catalog.get` also work when they resolve to a movie or episode.
For shows, send individual episode keys. The host checks viewer access and
writes through Ether's shared watch state. The SDK write takes a boolean.

```js
ether.viewers.setWatchState({ viewerId, titleId: itemRef, watched: true });
```

Subscribe with the `events` capability and `contributes.events.subscribe`.
Declare `viewers.identity: "granted_viewers"` to receive the viewer ID for
granted viewers. The `viewer.watch.scrobbled` subscription covers explicit marks
and playback completion. Alternatively, subscribe to `viewer.watch.watched`
and `viewer.watch.unwatched` for separate triggers, including current-state
updates from imports. `viewer.watch.progress` carries resume checkpoints in
`positionMs`. A plugin's writes are skipped when dispatching back to that plugin.

Events keep `titleKey` and `watched` and add `state` (`watched`, `unwatched`,
`progress`) and `source` (`playback`, `manual`, `plugin`, `import`). The
optional `surface` identifies the app or writing plugin. Use `itemRef` for your
own plugin's items. Catalogue events include available `tmdbId`, `tvdbId` and
`imdbId` fields. For episodes these are the series IDs, paired with `season`
and `episode`. Season zero represents specials.

// Catalogue returns the index URL and the key that must sign it: the
// owner's own catalogue when IndexURL is set, else the official marketplace.
// An owner URL is never paired with the official key.
func (p Plugins) Catalogue() (indexURL, publicKey string) {
	if url := strings.TrimSpace(p.IndexURL); url != "" {
		return url, strings.TrimSpace(p.PublicKey)
	}
	return OfficialCatalogueURL, OfficialCataloguePublicKey
}

// PluginRuntimeLimits are owner-controlled ceilings, not allocations. Zero
// inherits the default (globally) or the global ceiling (per plugin).
type PluginRuntimeLimits struct {
	// UploadBytes is the per-plugin staged request ceiling. Zero uses 64 MiB.

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#ValidExternalID

``````
// ValidExternalID reports whether id is a legal plugin external id
// (spec §2.2: ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._~-]{0,127}$, no ':' or '/').
func ValidExternalID(id string) bool {
	if len(id) == 0 || len(id) > 128 {
		return false
	}
	for i := 0; i < len(id); i++ {
		c := id[i]
		alnum := (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9')
		if i == 0 {
			if !alnum {
				return false
			}
			continue
		}
		if !alnum && c != '.' && c != '_' && c != '~' && c != '-' {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#ItemRef.Parse

``````
// Parse splits r into (pluginID, kindKey, externalID) and reports
// whether r is a well-formed ItemRef (spec §2.2).
func (r ItemRef) Parse() (pluginID, kindKey, externalID string, ok bool) {
	s, hasPrefix := strings.CutPrefix(string(r), "pk:")
	if !hasPrefix {
		return "", "", "", false
	}
	p1 := strings.IndexByte(s, ':')
	if p1 <= 0 {
		return "", "", "", false
	}
	pluginID = s[:p1]
	rest := s[p1+1:]
	p2 := strings.IndexByte(rest, ':')
	if p2 <= 0 {
		return "", "", "", false
	}
	kindKey = rest[:p2]
	externalID = rest[p2+1:]
	if strings.ContainsRune(pluginID, '/') || strings.ContainsRune(kindKey, '/') || !ValidExternalID(externalID) {
		return "", "", "", false
	}
	return pluginID, kindKey, externalID, true
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#ParseItemRef

``````
// ParseItemRef validates s and returns it as an ItemRef.
func ParseItemRef(s string) (ItemRef, error) {
	ref := ItemRef(s)
	if _, _, _, ok := ref.Parse(); !ok {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("itemRef %q: invalid format", s)
	}
	return ref, nil
}
``````

// Valid reports whether r is a well-formed ItemRef.

type KindItem struct {

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#ExtractKindItemPartsFromItem

``````
// ExtractKindItemPartsFromItem inspects a KindItem for declared parts,
// checking hints.parts first and falling back to a declared "parts" array
// field when present (#576).
func ExtractKindItemPartsFromItem(item KindItem) []KindItemPart {
	if parts := ExtractKindItemParts(item.Hints); len(parts) > 0 {
		return parts
	}
	if raw, ok := item.Fields["parts"]; ok && len(raw) > 0 {
		if wrapped, err := json.Marshal(struct {
			Parts json.RawMessage `json:"parts"`
		}{Parts: raw}); err == nil {
			return ExtractKindItemParts(wrapped)
		}
	}
	return nil
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#ExtractKindItemParts

``````
// ExtractKindItemParts inspects a KindItem's Hints JSON for a non-empty
// "parts" array and returns generic per-part metadata in declaration order.
// Returns nil when the item does not declare parts.
func ExtractKindItemParts(hints json.RawMessage) []KindItemPart {
	if len(hints) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	var env struct {
		Parts []json.RawMessage `json:"parts"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(hints, &env); err != nil || len(env.Parts) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]KindItemPart, 0, len(env.Parts))
	for i, raw := range env.Parts {
		part := KindItemPart{Index: i}
		var str string
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &str); err == nil {
			part.Name = strings.TrimSpace(str)
			out = append(out, part)
			continue
		}
		var obj struct {
			Name        string  `json:"name"`
			File        string  `json:"file"`
			Filename    string  `json:"filename"`
			Path        string  `json:"path"`
			ROM         string  `json:"rom"`
			Label       string  `json:"label"`
			Title       string  `json:"title"`
			ID          string  `json:"id"`
			MIME        string  `json:"mime"`
			MIMEType    string  `json:"mimeType"`
			ContentType string  `json:"contentType"`
			Size        int64   `json:"size"`
			SizeBytes   int64   `json:"sizeBytes"`
			ByteSize    int64   `json:"byteSize"`
			DurationSec float64 `json:"durationSec"`
			Duration    float64 `json:"duration"`
			FileIndex   *int    `json:"fileIndex"`
		}
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &obj); err == nil {
			for _, cand := range []string{obj.Name, obj.File, obj.Filename, obj.Path, obj.ROM, obj.Label, obj.Title, obj.ID} {
				if s := strings.TrimSpace(cand); s != "" {
					part.Name = s
					break
				}
			}
			for _, cand := range []string{obj.MIME, obj.MIMEType, obj.ContentType} {
				if s := strings.TrimSpace(cand); s != "" {
					part.MIME = s
					break
				}
			}
			for _, sz := range []int64{obj.Size, obj.SizeBytes, obj.ByteSize} {
				if sz > 0 {
					part.Size = sz
					break
				}
			}
			for _, dur := range []float64{obj.DurationSec, obj.Duration} {
				if dur > 0 {
					part.DurationSec = dur
					break
				}
			}
			if obj.FileIndex != nil && *obj.FileIndex >= 0 {
				v := *obj.FileIndex
				part.FileIndex = &v
			}
		}
		out = append(out, part)
	}
	return out
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#ExtractKindItemChaptersFromItem

``````
// ExtractKindItemChaptersFromItem inspects a KindItem for declared chapters,
// checking hints.chapters first and falling back to a declared "chapters" array
// field when present.
func ExtractKindItemChaptersFromItem(item KindItem) []Chapter {
	if chs := ExtractKindItemChapters(item.Hints); len(chs) > 0 {
		return chs
	}
	if raw, ok := item.Fields["chapters"]; ok && len(raw) > 0 {
		if wrapped, err := json.Marshal(struct {
			Chapters json.RawMessage `json:"chapters"`
		}{Chapters: raw}); err == nil {
			return ExtractKindItemChapters(wrapped)
		}
	}
	return nil
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#ExtractKindItemChapters

``````
// ExtractKindItemChapters inspects a KindItem's Hints JSON for a non-empty
// "chapters" array and returns normalized Chapter markers in declaration order.
func ExtractKindItemChapters(hints json.RawMessage) []Chapter {
	if len(hints) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	var env struct {
		Chapters []json.RawMessage `json:"chapters"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(hints, &env); err != nil || len(env.Chapters) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]Chapter, 0, len(env.Chapters))
	var cursor float64
	for i, raw := range env.Chapters {
		var obj struct {
			Title        string   `json:"title"`
			Name         string   `json:"name"`
			Label        string   `json:"label"`
			StartSec     *float64 `json:"startSec"`
			StartSeconds *float64 `json:"startSeconds"`
			Start        *float64 `json:"start"`
			EndSec       *float64 `json:"endSec"`
			EndSeconds   *float64 `json:"endSeconds"`
			End          *float64 `json:"end"`
			DurationSec  *float64 `json:"durationSec"`
			Duration     *float64 `json:"duration"`
		}
		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &obj); err != nil {
			continue
		}
		title := ""
		for _, cand := range []string{obj.Title, obj.Name, obj.Label} {
			if s := strings.TrimSpace(cand); s != "" {
				title = s
				break
			}
		}
		var startSec float64
		hasStart := false
		for _, cand := range []*float64{obj.StartSec, obj.StartSeconds, obj.Start} {
			if cand != nil && *cand >= 0 {
				startSec = *cand
				hasStart = true
				break
			}
		}
		if !hasStart {
			startSec = cursor
		}
		var endSec float64
		for _, cand := range []*float64{obj.EndSec, obj.EndSeconds, obj.End} {
			if cand != nil && *cand > startSec {
				endSec = *cand
				break
			}
		}
		if endSec <= startSec {
			for _, cand := range []*float64{obj.DurationSec, obj.Duration} {
				if cand != nil && *cand > 0 {
					endSec = startSec + *cand
					break
				}
			}
		}
		if endSec <= startSec && !hasStart && title == "" {
			continue
		}
		if title == "" {
			title = fmt.Sprintf("Chapter %d", i+1)
		}
		if endSec > cursor {
			cursor = endSec
		}
		out = append(out, Chapter{
			ID:    int64(i),
			Title: title,
			Start: time.Duration(startSec * float64(time.Second)),
			End:   time.Duration(endSec * float64(time.Second)),
		})
	}
	return out
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#KindBrowseFacetGroup

``````
// KindBrowseFacetGroup is one OR-group for KindBrowseRequest.AnyGroups (#767, #807).
// A group either names a single {field, values} OR-list or carries a list of
// {field, values} alternatives in Any that are ORed together across fields
// (and ANDed with the rest). Multiple groups — including repeated groups on
// the same field — combine with AND alongside Facets, AllFacets,
// ExcludeFacets, Empty, and ExcludeQuery.
type KindBrowseFacetGroup struct {
	Field  string               `json:"field,omitempty"`
	Values []string             `json:"values,omitempty"`
	Any    []KindBrowseFacetAlt `json:"any,omitempty"`
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#KindBrowseFacetGroup.Alternatives

``````
// Alternatives returns the {field, values} alternatives carried by g. A
// single-field {field, values} group returns a slice of one; when Any is
// present, its alternatives are returned (after the top-level field/values if
// both were supplied).
func (g KindBrowseFacetGroup) Alternatives() []KindBrowseFacetAlt {
	hasSingle := strings.TrimSpace(g.Field) != "" && len(g.Values) > 0
	if len(g.Any) == 0 {
		if !hasSingle {
			return nil
		}
		return []KindBrowseFacetAlt{{Field: g.Field, Values: g.Values}}
	}
	if !hasSingle {
		return g.Any
	}
	out := make([]KindBrowseFacetAlt, 0, len(g.Any)+1)
	out = append(out, KindBrowseFacetAlt{Field: g.Field, Values: g.Values})
	out = append(out, g.Any...)
	return out
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#KindBrowseRequest

``````
// KindBrowseRequest is the request body sent to a catalog_provider
// browse or search route (spec §3.1, §3.2) and passed to the
// viewer-scoped kinds.browse host service (#615).
type KindBrowseRequest struct {
	ParentID string `json:"parentId,omitempty"`
	Level    string `json:"level,omitempty"`
	Cursor   string `json:"cursor,omitempty"`
	Limit    int    `json:"limit,omitempty"`
	Sort     string `json:"sort,omitempty"`
	Desc     bool   `json:"desc,omitempty"`
	// Facets requires any of the listed values per field (OR within a
	// field, AND across fields). AllFacets requires every listed value
	// per field, ExcludeFacets drops items having any listed value, and
	// AnyGroups adds one OR-group per entry — either a single {field,
	// values} list or {any: [{field, values}, ...]} ORed across fields
	// (#767, #807). All four combine with AND and accept the same
	// per-type values (including lo..hi ranges and people names).
	Facets        map[string][]string    `json:"facets,omitempty"`
	AllFacets     map[string][]string    `json:"allFacets,omitempty"`
	ExcludeFacets map[string][]string    `json:"excludeFacets,omitempty"`
	AnyGroups     []KindBrowseFacetGroup `json:"anyGroups,omitempty"`
	// Empty tests field presence or absence per field key (#807): true
	// keeps items with no value in the field, false keeps items with at
	// least one. Counts toward neither facet value bound; unknown fields
	// are rejected.
	Empty map[string]bool `json:"empty,omitempty"`
	Query string          `json:"query,omitempty"`
	// ExcludeQuery drops items whose indexed text matches, using the same
	// text matching as Query (#807).
	ExcludeQuery string `json:"excludeQuery,omitempty"`
	// Total controls whether kinds.browse computes KindPage.Total (#682):
	//   - "" or "cheap" (default): populate Total only when O(1) (item or
	//     field tallies, a cached exact count, or a single-page result) and
	//     omit Total otherwise instead of running a full COUNT(*).
	//   - "none": never compute or return Total.
	//   - "exact": compute an exact Total (cached per library generation).
	Total string `json:"total,omitempty"`
}
``````

// EffectiveCursor returns Cursor when non-empty, falling back to NextCursor.
func (r KindExpandResponse) EffectiveCursor() string {

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#SourceQuery

``````
// SourceQuery asks Ether to find sources for a kind resolver
// (spec §4.5).
type SourceQuery struct {
	Kind  string `json:"kind"` // indexer_search|indexer_search_results|indexer_search_cancel|indexers|debrid|debrid_check|debrid_acquire|release_files|usenet_check|nzb_request
	Query string `json:"query,omitempty"`
	// Category accepts comma-separated Newznab IDs or standard family names.
	// When set with an empty Query, indexer_search requests recent releases.
	Category string `json:"category,omitempty"`
	// Lookup, on an indexer_search with a Category, adds a typed lookup
	// (e.g. {type: "album", fields: {artist, title}}) for plugin sources that
	// declared it. Every other indexer searches Query alone.
	Lookup *SourceLookup `json:"lookup,omitempty"`
	// Profile names the quality profile to score video release names against
	// on indexer_search; empty uses the owner's default profile.
	Profile    string   `json:"profile,omitempty"`
	InfoHashes []string `json:"infoHashes,omitempty"`
	InfoHash   string   `json:"infoHash,omitempty"`
	Magnet     string   `json:"magnet,omitempty"`
	// TorrentURL carries a torrent download or details page link for torrent
	// indexers that do not emit an info hash or magnet in search results.
	TorrentURL string `json:"torrentUrl,omitempty"`
	TorrentRef string `json:"torrentRef,omitempty"`
	// NZBURL carries a Usenet NZB link for usenet_check when the plugin does
	// not pass a full Candidate from indexer_search.
	NZBURL      string       `json:"nzbUrl,omitempty"`
	NZBRef      string       `json:"nzbRef,omitempty"`
	NZBIdentity *NZBIdentity `json:"nzbIdentity,omitempty"`
	// Candidate carries a candidate previously returned by indexer_search
	// back for release_files or usenet_check, so an NZB or torrent link is
	// resolved through its originating indexer.
	Candidate *SourceCandidate `json:"candidate,omitempty"`
	// FileCount optionally hints how many files a torrent contains when Ether
	// has not seen its file list yet (e.g. a magnet for a large collection),
	// so zip-only debrid caches are checked via cached-only add.
	FileCount int `json:"fileCount,omitempty"`
	// Stream, when true on indexer_search, starts the indexer fan-out and
	// returns immediately with a searchId handle to poll via
	// indexer_search_results or stop via indexer_search_cancel.
	Stream bool `json:"stream,omitempty"`
	// SearchID identifies a streaming search started by indexer_search with
	// stream:true; required on indexer_search_results and indexer_search_cancel.
	SearchID string `json:"searchId,omitempty"`
	// WaitMS sets how long indexer_search_results waits (in milliseconds,
	// capped at 10000 ms) for at least one new arrival or search completion
	// before returning. Zero returns immediately with arrivals buffered so far.
	WaitMS int `json:"waitMs,omitempty"`
	// FirstResults, when true on indexer_search, returns early as soon as the
	// fastest indexer(s) return results plus the SettleMS window (default
	// 250 ms; 0 returns immediately), while slower indexers keep running in the
	// background to populate Ether's search cache for later calls. Default
	// false waits for every searched indexer.
	FirstResults bool `json:"firstResults,omitempty"`
	// SettleMS sets the settle window in milliseconds after the first results
	// arrive under FirstResults (default 250 ms when nil; 0 returns
	// immediately), or after MinResults is met when FirstResults is false.
	// Clamped to the effective call timeout.
	SettleMS *int `json:"settleMs,omitempty"`
	// MinResults sets a minimum deduplicated candidate count for early return
	// on indexer_search. Once at least MinResults unique results have arrived,
	// Ether returns early while remaining indexers keep filling Ether's search
	// cache. Combined with FirstResults, returns as soon as either MinResults
	// is reached or the settle window elapses.
	MinResults int `json:"minResults,omitempty"`
	// SkipIndexers excludes matching enabled indexers from an indexer_search
	// fan-out by indexerId or indexer name (case-insensitive, trimmed).
	SkipIndexers []string `json:"skipIndexers,omitempty"`
	// OnlyIndexers, when non-empty, restricts an indexer_search fan-out to
	// matching enabled indexers by indexerId or indexer name (case-insensitive,
	// trimmed). Entries also matching SkipIndexers are excluded.
	OnlyIndexers []string `json:"onlyIndexers,omitempty"`
	// TimeoutMS sets a per-call wait limit in milliseconds for indexer_search,
	// capped by Ether's 30 s indexer-search ceiling and any shorter route
	// deadline. When TimeoutMS is shorter than the ceiling and expires while
	// slow indexers keep filling the search cache, those indexers are reported
	// as pending (and listed in top-level pending); indexers that hit the 30 s
	// ceiling are reported as timed_out. Omit or 0 keeps the 30 s default.
	TimeoutMS int `json:"timeoutMs,omitempty"`
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#IndexerSearchStatus.MarshalJSON

``````
// MarshalJSON preserves ms:0 on search status entries (Status != "") while
// omitting status/ms/results/reason/error on kind:"indexers" listing entries
// (Status == "").
func (s IndexerSearchStatus) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
	if s.Status == "" {
		type listing struct {
			IndexerID string `json:"indexerId"`
			Indexer   string `json:"indexer"`
			Kind      string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
			MedianMS  *int64 `json:"medianMs,omitempty"`
			LastMS    *int64 `json:"lastMs,omitempty"`
			LastError string `json:"lastError,omitempty"`
		}
		return json.Marshal(listing{
			IndexerID: s.IndexerID,
			Indexer:   s.Indexer,
			Kind:      s.Kind,
			MedianMS:  s.MedianMS,
			LastMS:    s.LastMS,
			LastError: s.LastError,
		})
	}
	type searchStatus struct {
		IndexerID string `json:"indexerId"`
		Indexer   string `json:"indexer"`
		Status    string `json:"status"`
		Results   int    `json:"results,omitempty"`
		MS        int64  `json:"ms"`
		Reason    string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
		Error     string `json:"error,omitempty"`
		Kind      string `json:"kind,omitempty"`
		MedianMS  *int64 `json:"medianMs,omitempty"`
		LastMS    *int64 `json:"lastMs,omitempty"`
		LastError string `json:"lastError,omitempty"`
	}
	return json.Marshal(searchStatus{
		IndexerID: s.IndexerID,
		Indexer:   s.Indexer,
		Status:    s.Status,
		Results:   s.Results,
		MS:        s.MS,
		Reason:    s.Reason,
		Error:     s.Error,
		Kind:      s.Kind,
		MedianMS:  s.MedianMS,
		LastMS:    s.LastMS,
		LastError: s.LastError,
	})
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#SourceResolveResult.MarshalJSON

``````
// MarshalJSON emits the debrid policy by itself for the debrid query.
// Candidate queries always emit candidates and preserve non-nil empty search
// slices as [].
func (r SourceResolveResult) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
	if r.Enabled != nil {
		return json.Marshal(struct {
			Enabled    bool  `json:"enabled"`
			CachedOnly *bool `json:"cachedOnly"`
		}{Enabled: *r.Enabled, CachedOnly: r.CachedOnly})
	}
	cands := r.Candidates
	if cands == nil {
		cands = []SourceCandidate{}
	}
	wire := struct {
		Candidates []SourceCandidate      `json:"candidates"`
		CachedOnly *bool                  `json:"cachedOnly,omitempty"`
		Indexers   *[]IndexerSearchStatus `json:"indexers,omitempty"`
		Pending    *[]IndexerRef          `json:"pending,omitempty"`
		SearchID   string                 `json:"searchId,omitempty"`
		Done       *bool                  `json:"done,omitempty"`
	}{
		Candidates: cands,
		CachedOnly: r.CachedOnly,
		SearchID:   r.SearchID,
		Done:       r.Done,
	}
	if r.Indexers != nil {
		s := r.Indexers
		wire.Indexers = &s
	}
	if r.Pending != nil {
		s := r.Pending
		wire.Pending = &s
	}
	return json.Marshal(wire)
}
``````

// ReleaseFile is one file inside a candidate release, as returned by a

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#SourceCandidate

``````
// SourceCandidate is one Ether-found release for a resolver to rank,
// carrying the release-hint fields plus the facts matching needs.
// Torrent candidates carry their infoHash, magnet, and/or torrentUrl and never
// populate nzbUrl; Usenet candidates populate nzbUrl. Same-origin download
// links returned by indexer_search are stripped of indexer API keys and
// secrets (Ether re-attaches them at fetch time on the originating indexer's
// origin), so plugins can safely cache candidates without storing credentials.
type SourceCandidate struct {
	InfoHash   string `json:"infoHash,omitempty"`
	Magnet     string `json:"magnet,omitempty"`
	TorrentURL string `json:"torrentUrl,omitempty"`
	TorrentRef string `json:"torrentRef,omitempty"`
	NZBURL     string `json:"nzbUrl,omitempty"`
	NZBRef     string `json:"nzbRef,omitempty"`
	// FileIndex selects a zero-based entry in the torrent provider file list; nil uses video selection.
	FileIndex *int   `json:"fileIndex,omitempty"`
	Title     string `json:"title,omitempty"`
	Size      int64  `json:"size,omitempty"`
	Seeders   int    `json:"seeders,omitempty"`
	Cached    bool   `json:"cached,omitempty"`
	// CachedBy lists the owner-configured debrid services holding this
	// torrent in the order Ether would acquire from them (or, on
	// debrid_acquire, the service that served it). Omitted when uncached.
	CachedBy []DebridServiceRef `json:"cachedBy,omitempty"`
	// Indexer and IndexerID name the indexer an indexer_search result came
	// from, so a plugin that hands the candidate back can be fetched
	// through that indexer (an NZB needs its originating indexer).
	Indexer   string `json:"indexer,omitempty"`
	IndexerID string `json:"indexerId,omitempty"`
	// Category is the standard Newznab/Torznab category ID reported for this
	// release when known, preserving media type for follow-up downloads.
	Category int `json:"category,omitempty"`
	// Score, Resolution, Source and Codec are populated on indexer_search
	// candidates whose release name identifies video, scored against the
	// requested (or owner default) quality profile; non-video candidates
	// leave them empty.
	Score      *int   `json:"score,omitempty"`
	Resolution int    `json:"resolution,omitempty"`
	Source     string `json:"source,omitempty"`
	Codec      string `json:"codec,omitempty"`
	// Files is populated by release_files and nzb_request: the files inside
	// this candidate release.
	Files []ReleaseFile `json:"files,omitempty"`
	// FileCount is the torrent's known file count when reported by an indexer
	// or release_files query, allowing zip-only debrid caches to be probed by
	// cached-only add even when Files is omitted.
	FileCount int `json:"fileCount,omitempty"`
	// UsenetCheck is populated only by a usenet_check query: the sampled
	// article availability verdict and any recorded playback failure for
	// this NZB release.
	UsenetCheck *UsenetCheckResult `json:"usenetCheck,omitempty"`
	// PluginRelease names a release a stream_source plugin answered for a
	// category search it declared (ether.contributes.source.search). It has
	// no info hash, magnet or NZB: release_files asks that plugin for the
	// files and a release source opens it through the plugin's open route.
	PluginRelease *PluginReleaseRef `json:"pluginRelease,omitempty"`
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#PluginLibraryKey

``````
// PluginLibraryKey is the library key a plugin kind owns
// (spec §1.1): "pk-" + slug(pluginID) + "-" + slug(kindKey), matching
// internal/libraries.UpsertPluginLibrary. The key is an opaque unique
// slug; ownership is always read back from the stored plugin/kind
// columns, never parsed out of the key.
func PluginLibraryKey(pluginID, kindKey string) string {
	return "pk-" + libraryKeySlug(pluginID) + "-" + libraryKeySlug(kindKey)
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#libraryKeySlug

``````
func libraryKeySlug(s string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	dash := false
	for _, r := range strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)) {
		switch {
		case unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.IsDigit(r):
			if dash && b.Len() > 0 {
				b.WriteByte('-')
			}
			dash = false
			b.WriteRune(r)
		default:
			dash = true
		}
	}
	return b.String()
}
``````

Sources in different tiers keep the plugin's tier order; when Tier is nil, the plugin's exact order is kept. |

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#PlayableSource

``````
// PlayableSource is one candidate way to acquire bytes for a KindItem or one of
// its parts (spec §4.1). Multiple sources are tried in order.
type PlayableSource struct {
	// Connections requests up to six parallel reads of a range source. Zero uses one.
	Connections int    `json:"connections,omitempty"`
	Path        string `json:"path,omitempty"`
	ID          string `json:"id"`
	Label       string `json:"label,omitempty"`
	Pattern     string `json:"pattern"` // "range" | "download" | "direct" | "container" | "release" | "file"
	MIME        string `json:"mime"`
	// Tier optionally marks interchangeable sources of the same quality tier.
	// Sources sharing a non-nil Tier may be reordered by Ether's source routing
	// (owner preference, measured startup, and stall demotion) and may overtake
	// each other after the ranked open grace period. Sources in different tiers
	// keep the plugin's tier order; when Tier is nil, the plugin's exact order
	// is kept.
	Tier *int  `json:"tier,omitempty"`
	Size int64 `json:"size,omitempty"`
	// SizeApproximate marks Size as an approximate hint (for example from a
	// Usenet release_files estimate) rather than an exact byte count:
	// kindstream applies a tolerance band instead of failing on exact byte
	// inequality, while exact sizes (false/omitted) remain strict.
	SizeApproximate bool    `json:"sizeApproximate,omitempty"`
	DurationSec     float64 `json:"durationSec,omitempty"`
	// DurationToleranceSec opts into open-time container duration verification:
	// when both DurationSec and DurationToleranceSec are positive, Ether reads
	// the container duration (reusing the durable release_probes cache when
	// available) and refuses the source as wrong content (core.ErrWrongContent
	// / kindstream.ErrPluginAnswer) when the observed duration differs from
	// DurationSec by more than DurationToleranceSec seconds, so the next
	// candidate is tried. Omitted or zero leaves DurationSec as estimated
	// metadata only.
	DurationToleranceSec float64           `json:"durationToleranceSec,omitempty"`
	URL                  string            `json:"url,omitempty"`
	Headers              map[string]string `json:"headers,omitempty"`
	// KeepHeadersOnRedirect lists optional host or wildcard (*.example.org)
	// patterns (within permissions.network / granted hosts) that may keep
	// credentials and caller headers across redirects when the target is not
	// already the same origin or a strict same-site subdomain. Never applies
	// across HTTPS -> HTTP downgrades.
	KeepHeadersOnRedirect []string `json:"keepHeadersOnRedirect,omitempty"`
	BlobRef               string   `json:"blobRef,omitempty"`
	SHA256                string   `json:"sha256,omitempty"`
	// SHA1 and CRC32 are the digests content catalogues actually publish
	// (hex; CRC32 is the IEEE polynomial as 8 hex digits). Any declared
	// digest — and Size, when set — is checked against the bytes actually
	// served, including a release's selected file or container member.
	SHA1      string         `json:"sha1,omitempty"`
	CRC32     string         `json:"crc32,omitempty"`
	MaxBytes  int64          `json:"maxBytes,omitempty"`
	ExpiresAt int64          `json:"expiresAt,omitempty"`
	Container *ContainerRef  `json:"container,omitempty"`
	Release   *ReleaseHint   `json:"release,omitempty"`
	Parts     []KindItemPart `json:"parts,omitempty"`
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/kinditem.go#ReleaseHint

``````
// ReleaseHint hands an NZB, magnet, infohash, torrent link, or pre-built
// Candidate to Ether's existing Usenet / debrid / torrent acquisition pipeline
// (spec §4.1, §4.3).
type ReleaseHint struct {
	// FileIndex overrides candidate.fileIndex; out-of-range indices fail without fallback.
	FileIndex  *int             `json:"fileIndex,omitempty"`
	NZBURL     string           `json:"nzbUrl,omitempty"`
	NZBRef     string           `json:"nzbRef,omitempty"`
	Magnet     string           `json:"magnet,omitempty"`
	InfoHash   string           `json:"infoHash,omitempty"`
	TorrentURL string           `json:"torrentUrl,omitempty"`
	TorrentRef string           `json:"torrentRef,omitempty"`
	Candidate  *SourceCandidate `json:"candidate,omitempty"`
	// File selects an exact torrent path or unique basename, including non-video files.
	File           string     `json:"file,omitempty"`
	FileHint       string     `json:"fileHint,omitempty"`
	Track          *TrackHint `json:"track,omitempty"`
	PasswordSecret string     `json:"passwordSecret,omitempty"`
	// CachedOnly forces debrid acquisition to require an already-cached copy
	// even when the owner turned "Cached torrents only" off. When omitted or
	// false, torrent releases follow the owner's debrid setting (queuing
	// uncached downloads when cached-only is off).
	CachedOnly bool `json:"cachedOnly,omitempty"`
	// FileCount optionally hints how many files a torrent contains when Ether
	// has not seen its file list yet (for example a magnet for one entry in a
	// large collection). Providers whose cache check cannot see zip-only
	// high-file-count torrents (such as TorBox at 100+ files) use this to try
	// a cached-only add instead of trusting a checkcached miss.
	FileCount int `json:"fileCount,omitempty"`
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/liveevent.go#ValidLiveEventState

``````
// ValidLiveEventState reports whether s is a defined LiveEventStatus.State value.
func ValidLiveEventState(s string) bool {
	switch s {
	case LiveEventStatePre, LiveEventStateIn, LiveEventStatePost,
		LiveEventStateDelayed, LiveEventStatePostponed, LiveEventStateCanceled:
		return true
	default:
		return false
	}
}

## Source: internal/core/liveevent.go#NamespaceLiveEventID

``````
// NamespaceLiveEventID constructs Ether's globally unique event ID:
// "pluginID:feedID:eventID". Plugins always use their own feed-scoped ID;
// Ether namespaces it at the hub boundary.
func NamespaceLiveEventID(pluginID, feedID, eventID string) string {
	return pluginID + ":" + feedID + ":" + eventID
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/liveevent.go#ParseLiveEventID

``````
// ParseLiveEventID splits a namespaced event ID ("pluginID:feedID:eventID")
// into its plugin ID, feed ID, and plugin-scoped event ID.
func ParseLiveEventID(namespaced string) (pluginID, feedID, eventID string, ok bool) {
	p, rest, ok1 := strings.Cut(namespaced, ":")
	if !ok1 || p == "" || strings.ContainsAny(p, "/ \t\r\n") {
		return "", "", "", false
	}
	f, id, ok2 := strings.Cut(rest, ":")
	if !ok2 || f == "" || id == "" || strings.ContainsAny(f, "/ \t\r\n") {
		return "", "", "", false
	}
	return p, f, id, true
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/liveevent.go#NamespaceLiveEntityKey

``````
// NamespaceLiveEntityKey constructs Ether's globally unique entity key:
// "pluginID:feedID:entityKind:entityID".
func NamespaceLiveEntityKey(pluginID, feedID, entityKind, entityID string) string {
	return pluginID + ":" + feedID + ":" + entityKind + ":" + entityID
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/liveevent.go#ParseLiveEntityKey

``````
// ParseLiveEntityKey splits a namespaced entity key
// ("pluginID:feedID:entityKind:entityID") into its four components.
func ParseLiveEntityKey(key string) (pluginID, feedID, entityKind, entityID string, ok bool) {
	p, rest1, ok1 := strings.Cut(key, ":")
	if !ok1 || p == "" || strings.ContainsAny(p, "/ \t\r\n") {
		return "", "", "", "", false
	}
	f, rest2, ok2 := strings.Cut(rest1, ":")
	if !ok2 || f == "" || strings.ContainsAny(f, "/ \t\r\n") {
		return "", "", "", "", false
	}
	kind, id, ok3 := strings.Cut(rest2, ":")
	if !ok3 || kind == "" || id == "" || strings.ContainsAny(kind, "/ \t\r\n") {
		return "", "", "", "", false
	}
	return p, f, kind, id, true
}
``````

// channels are currently unhealthy so clients can show "Unavailable right now".
type LiveEventWatchProgramme struct {
	ArchiveDays int       `json:"-"`
	ID          string    `json:"id"`
	Start       time.Time `json:"start"`
	End         time.Time `json:"end"`
	CatchUp     bool      `json:"catchUp,omitempty"`
	StartOver   bool      `json:"startOver,omitempty"`
}

// IsAvailable reports whether the watch target is currently playable

## Source: internal/core/liveevent.go#LiveEventWatchTarget.Clone

``````
// Clone returns a deep copy of t including its availability flag and any
// collapsed alternate feeds.
func (t LiveEventWatchTarget) Clone() LiveEventWatchTarget {
	out := t
	if t.Programme != nil {
		programme := *t.Programme
		out.Programme = &programme
	}
	if t.Available != nil {
		av := *t.Available
		out.Available = &av
	}
	if len(t.Alternates) > 0 {
		out.Alternates = make([]LiveEventWatchTarget, len(t.Alternates))
		for i, alt := range t.Alternates {
			out.Alternates[i] = alt.Clone()
		}
	}
	return out
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/liveevent.go#LiveEvent.Clone

``````
// Clone returns a deep copy of e so callers may apply viewer-specific filters
// without mutating shared cached state.
func (e LiveEvent) Clone() LiveEvent {
	out := e
	if len(e.Competitors) > 0 {
		out.Competitors = append([]LiveEventCompetitor(nil), e.Competitors...)
	} else {
		out.Competitors = []LiveEventCompetitor{}
	}
	if e.Ranking != nil {
		out.Ranking = append([]LiveEventRankRow(nil), e.Ranking...)
	}
	if e.Situation != nil {
		out.Situation = make(map[string]string, len(e.Situation))
		for k, v := range e.Situation {
			out.Situation[k] = v
		}
	}
	if e.Probability != nil {
		p := *e.Probability
		out.Probability = &p
	}
	if e.Broadcasts != nil {
		out.Broadcasts = append([]LiveEventBroadcast(nil), e.Broadcasts...)
	}
	if e.MatchHints != nil {
		h := &LiveEventMatchHints{}
		if e.MatchHints.Terms != nil {
			h.Terms = append([]string(nil), e.MatchHints.Terms...)
		}
		if e.MatchHints.Callsigns != nil {
			h.Callsigns = append([]string(nil), e.MatchHints.Callsigns...)
		}
		out.MatchHints = h
	}
	if e.Watch != nil {
		out.Watch = make([]LiveEventWatchTarget, len(e.Watch))
		for i, w := range e.Watch {
			out.Watch[i] = w.Clone()
		}
	}
	return out
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/liveevent.go#LiveEventTable.Clone

``````
// Clone returns a deep copy of t.
func (t LiveEventTable) Clone() LiveEventTable {
	out := LiveEventTable{Title: t.Title}
	if len(t.RowEntityIDs) > 0 {
		out.RowEntityIDs = append([]string(nil), t.RowEntityIDs...)
	}
	if len(t.Columns) > 0 {
		out.Columns = append([]string(nil), t.Columns...)
	} else {
		out.Columns = []string{}
	}
	if len(t.Rows) > 0 {
		out.Rows = make([][]string, len(t.Rows))
		for i, row := range t.Rows {
			if len(row) > 0 {
				out.Rows[i] = append([]string(nil), row...)
			} else {
				out.Rows[i] = []string{}
			}
		}
	} else {
		out.Rows = [][]string{}
	}
	return out
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/liveevent.go#*LiveEventProbabilityTime.UnmarshalJSON

``````
// UnmarshalJSON accepts either a JSON number (0..1 game fraction) or a JSON string (RFC3339 timestamp).
func (t *LiveEventProbabilityTime) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error {
	trimmed := bytes.TrimSpace(data)
	if len(trimmed) == 0 || bytes.Equal(trimmed, []byte("null")) {
		*t = LiveEventProbabilityTime{}
		return nil
	}
	if trimmed[0] == '"' {
		var s string
		if err := json.Unmarshal(trimmed, &s); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		*t = LiveEventProbabilityTime{Time: s}
		return nil
	}
	var num float64
	if err := json.Unmarshal(trimmed, &num); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("probability point t must be a 0..1 number or RFC3339 string: %w", err)
	}
	*t = LiveEventProbabilityTime{Fraction: &num}
	return nil
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/liveevent.go#LiveEventDetail.MarshalJSON

``````
// MarshalJSON preserves embedded LiveEvent fields while guaranteeing
// spec-required array fields (competitors) encode as [].
func (d LiveEventDetail) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
	type liveEventAlias LiveEvent
	type wire struct {
		liveEventAlias
		Tables            []LiveEventTable            `json:"tables,omitempty"`
		Plays             []LiveEventPlay             `json:"plays,omitempty"`
		ProbabilitySeries []LiveEventProbabilityPoint `json:"probabilitySeries,omitempty"`
		Links             []LiveEventLink             `json:"links,omitempty"`
	}
	base := liveEventAlias(d.LiveEvent)
	if base.Competitors == nil {
		base.Competitors = []LiveEventCompetitor{}
	}
	return json.Marshal(wire{
		liveEventAlias:    base,
		Tables:            d.Tables,
		Plays:             d.Plays,
		ProbabilitySeries: d.ProbabilitySeries,
		Links:             d.Links,
	})
}
``````

## Source: internal/core/liveevent.go#LiveEventDetail.Clone

``````
// Clone returns a deep copy of d.
func (d LiveEventDetail) Clone() LiveEventDetail {
	out := LiveEventDetail{
		LiveEvent: d.LiveEvent.Clone(),
	}
	if d.Tables != nil {
		out.Tables = make([]LiveEventTable, len(d.Tables))
		for i, tbl := range d.Tables {
			out.Tables[i] = tbl.Clone()
		}
	}
	if d.Plays != nil {
		out.Plays = make([]LiveEventPlay, len(d.Plays))
		for i, p := range d.Plays {
			out.Plays[i] = p
			if p.Score != nil {
				out.Plays[i].Score = make(map[string]string, len(p.Score))
				for k, v := range p.Score {
					out.Plays[i].Score[k] = v
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if d.ProbabilitySeries != nil {
		out.ProbabilitySeries = make([]LiveEventProbabilityPoint, len(d.ProbabilitySeries))
		for i, pt := range d.ProbabilitySeries {
			out.ProbabilitySeries[i] = LiveEventProbabilityPoint{T: pt.T.Clone(), Value: pt.Value}
		}
	}
	if d.Links != nil {
		out.Links = append([]LiveEventLink(nil), d.Links...)
	}
	return out
}
``````

// sync) in the plugin's job list so Activity and Overview show live progress

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*HostJobHandle.SetProgress

``````
// SetProgress updates the human-readable progress line on a host-tracked job.
func (h *HostJobHandle) SetProgress(progress string) {
	if h == nil || h.job == nil {
		return
	}
	if len(progress) > 1024 {
		progress = progress[:1024]
	}
	h.job.mu.Lock()
	h.job.status.Progress = progress
	h.job.status.Attempts++
	h.job.mu.Unlock()
}

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*HostJobHandle.Finish

``````
// Finish marks a host-tracked job terminal with optional code, outcome and error.
func (h *HostJobHandle) Finish(state, code, outcome, errMsg string, failure *RouteFailure) {
	if h == nil || h.job == nil {
		return
	}
	now := time.Now().UTC()
	if h.m != nil && h.m.now != nil {
		now = h.m.now()
	}
	if len(outcome) > 1024 {
		outcome = outcome[:1024]
	}
	if len(errMsg) > 1024 {
		errMsg = errMsg[:1024]
	}
	h.job.mu.Lock()
	h.job.status.State = state
	h.job.status.Code = code
	h.job.status.Outcome = outcome
	h.job.status.Error = errMsg
	h.job.status.Failure = failure
	h.job.status.Finished = now
	if state == "done" {
		h.job.status.Progress = ""
	}
	h.job.mu.Unlock()
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.BeginHostJob

``````
// BeginHostJob records a host-managed background job for pluginID in m.jobs
// without consuming the plugin's ActionJobConcurrency slots. Cancelling the job
// from the Activity API calls cancel.
func (m *Manager) BeginHostJob(pluginID, dedupKey, routePath, label, kind string, cancel context.CancelFunc) *HostJobHandle {
	if m == nil || pluginID == "" || dedupKey == "" {
		return nil
	}
	if cancel == nil {
		cancel = func() {}
	}
	key := pluginID + "|host|" + dedupKey
	m.jobsMu.Lock()
	defer m.jobsMu.Unlock()
	count := 0
	oldestKey := ""
	var oldest time.Time
	m.jobs.Range(func(k, v any) bool {
		ks := k.(string)
		if !strings.HasPrefix(ks, pluginID+"|") {
			return true
		}
		s := v.(*actionJob).snapshot()
		if s.Code == frontendPreparationWaitCode {
			return true
		}
		count++
		if s.State != "running" && (oldestKey == "" || s.Started.Before(oldest)) {
			oldestKey, oldest = ks, s.Started
		}
		return true
	})
	if _, exists := m.jobs.Load(key); !exists && count >= 16 && oldestKey != "" {
		m.jobs.Delete(oldestKey)
	}
	started := time.Now().UTC()
	if m.now != nil {
		started = m.now()
	}
	done := make(chan struct{})
	close(done)
	j := &actionJob{
		cancel: cancel,
		done:   done,
		status: ActionJobStatus{
			Path:    routePath,
			Label:   label,
			Kind:    kind,
			State:   "running",
			Started: started,
		},
	}
	m.jobs.Store(key, j)
	return &HostJobHandle{m: m, pluginID: pluginID, job: j}
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.TrackFrontendPreparationWait

``````
// TrackFrontendPreparationWait adds a transient Activity row for a held
// download. Its cancellation stops the request wait, independently of the
// resolver job. The caller removes the row before delivering the stream.
func (m *Manager) TrackFrontendPreparationWait(pluginID string, budget time.Duration, cancel context.CancelFunc) func() {
	if m == nil {
		return func() {}
	}
	path := fmt.Sprintf("/ether/v1/kind-media/wait-%d", frontendPreparationWaitID.Add(1))
	key := pluginID + "|host|" + path
	done := make(chan struct{})
	close(done)
	m.jobs.Store(key, &actionJob{
		cancel: cancel,
		done:   done,
		status: ActionJobStatus{
			Path:         path,
			Code:         frontendPreparationWaitCode,
			State:        "running",
			Started:      time.Now().UTC(),
			TotalLimitMS: budget.Milliseconds(),
		},
	})
	return func() { m.jobs.Delete(key) }
}

``````
// UpdateHostJob updates an existing non-running host-managed job (for example
// when the owner acknowledges a paused delete guard and chooses to keep items).
func (m *Manager) UpdateHostJob(pluginID, dedupKey, state, code, outcome, errMsg string) {
	if m == nil || pluginID == "" || dedupKey == "" {
		return
	}
	key := pluginID + "|host|" + dedupKey
	v, ok := m.jobs.Load(key)
	if !ok {
		return
	}
	j := v.(*actionJob)
	now := time.Now().UTC()
	if m.now != nil {
		now = m.now()
	}
	j.mu.Lock()
	defer j.mu.Unlock()
	if j.status.State == "running" {
		return
	}
	j.status.State = state
	j.status.Code = code
	j.status.Outcome = outcome
	j.status.Error = errMsg
	j.status.Failure = nil
	j.status.Progress = ""
	j.status.Finished = now
}

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*ExpandJobRunner.Call

``````
// Call invokes a plugin route and increments the job's attempt counter. A fill
// always starts because a viewer opened that studio or person and is waiting
// for it, so it does not yield to other streams the way speculative background
// work does.
func (r *ExpandJobRunner) Call(ctx context.Context, req Request) (Response, error) {
	r.job.mu.Lock()
	r.job.status.Attempts++
	r.job.mu.Unlock()
	return r.m.Call(ctx, r.pluginID, req)
}

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*ExpandJobRunner.RunContinuation

``````
// RunContinuation drives a /ether/job/... continuation inside the same background
// job slot so long-running expansions never consume a second ActionJobConcurrency slot.
func (r *ExpandJobRunner) RunContinuation(ctx context.Context, jobPath string, initial json.RawMessage, onStep func(body json.RawMessage) error) error {
	path := strings.TrimSpace(jobPath)
	if !strings.HasPrefix(path, "/ether/job/") {
		path = "/ether/job/" + strings.TrimPrefix(path, "/")
	}
	if len(path) > 256 || strings.Contains(path, "..") || strings.ContainsAny(path, "?#\\") {
		return fmt.Errorf("invalid job path %q", jobPath)
	}
	redact := func(s string) string {
		if r.m == nil || r.m.store == nil {
			return logredact.String(s)
		}
		return r.m.store.redactKnown(context.Background(), r.pluginID, s)
	}
	return runActionJobWithHook(ctx, r.job, ActionJobAttempts, func(ctx context.Context, token json.RawMessage) (Response, error) {
		payload := map[string]json.RawMessage{}
		_ = json.Unmarshal(initial, &payload)
		if payload == nil {
			payload = map[string]json.RawMessage{}
		}
		if len(token) > 0 {
			payload["continuation"] = token
		}
		encoded, _ := json.Marshal(payload)
		return r.m.Call(WithBackgroundCall(ctx), r.pluginID, Request{Method: "POST", Path: path, Body: encoded})
	}, onStep, redact)
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.StartExpandJob

``````
// StartExpandJob starts a lowered-priority background expansion job for
// (pluginID, dedupKey) sharing the plugin's ActionJobConcurrency = 2 background
// pool (never ResolverJobConcurrency). If a job for dedupKey is already running,
// it returns started=false, err=nil. If two background jobs are already running
// for pluginID, it returns ErrJobsBusy.
func (m *Manager) StartExpandJob(pluginID, routePath, dedupKey string, fn func(ctx context.Context, run *ExpandJobRunner) error) (bool, error) {
	return m.StartExpandJobPriority(pluginID, routePath, dedupKey, false, fn)
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.StartExpandJobPriority

``````
// StartExpandJobPriority is StartExpandJob for an expansion a viewer is
// waiting on (an artist page being opened): it may use one slot beyond the
// background pool, so a viewer's open never waits behind background work.
func (m *Manager) StartExpandJobPriority(pluginID, routePath, dedupKey string, interactive bool, fn func(ctx context.Context, run *ExpandJobRunner) error) (bool, error) {
	if m == nil {
		return false, ErrUnavailable
	}
	key := pluginID + "|expand|" + dedupKey
	m.jobsMu.Lock()
	defer m.jobsMu.Unlock()
	if old, ok := m.jobs.Load(key); ok && old.(*actionJob).snapshot().State == "running" {
		return false, nil
	}
	resolverPrefix := pluginID + "|resolver|"
	hostPrefix := pluginID + "|host|"
	activeAction, count := 0, 0
	oldestKey := ""
	var oldest time.Time
	m.jobs.Range(func(k, v any) bool {
		ks := k.(string)
		if !strings.HasPrefix(ks, pluginID+"|") {
			return true
		}
		s := v.(*actionJob).snapshot()
		if s.Code == frontendPreparationWaitCode {
			return true
		}
		count++
		if s.State == "running" {
			if !strings.HasPrefix(ks, resolverPrefix) && !strings.HasPrefix(ks, hostPrefix) {
				activeAction++
			}
		} else if oldestKey == "" || s.Started.Before(oldest) {
			oldestKey, oldest = ks, s.Started
		}
		return true
	})
	limit := ActionJobConcurrency
	if interactive {
		limit++
	}
	if activeAction >= limit {
		return false, &core.JobsBusyError{Message: "Two background jobs are already running; wait for one to finish."}
	}
	if _, exists := m.jobs.Load(key); !exists && count >= 16 && oldestKey != "" {
		m.jobs.Delete(oldestKey)
	}
	started := time.Now().UTC()
	if m.now != nil {
		started = m.now()
	}
	ceilings := m.runtimeCeilings(pluginID)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), ceilings.deadline)
	j := &actionJob{
		cancel: cancel,
		done:   make(chan struct{}),
		status: ActionJobStatus{
			Path:         routePath,
			State:        "running",
			Started:      started,
			TotalLimitMS: ceilings.deadline.Milliseconds(),
			AttemptLimit: ActionJobAttempts,
		},
	}
	m.jobs.Store(key, j)
	go func() {
		runtime.LockOSThread() // Do not unlock: this lowered-priority thread is discarded on return.
		lowerJobPriority()
		defer cancel()
		defer close(j.done)
		err := fn(ctx, &ExpandJobRunner{m: m, pluginID: pluginID, job: j})
		if err != nil {
			state := "error"
			if ctx.Err() == context.Canceled {
				state = "canceled"
			}
			if ctx.Err() == context.DeadlineExceeded {
				err = fmt.Errorf("job reached its total time limit of %s", ceilings.deadline)
			}
			reason := m.store.redactKnown(context.Background(), pluginID, err.Error())
			j.finish(state, reason)
			m.log.Warn("plugins: expand job", "plugin", pluginID, "job", routePath, "err", reason)
			if state == "error" {
				durMS := max(time.Since(started).Milliseconds(), int64(0))
				m.emitBusEvent(events.EventPluginJobFailed, pluginID, events.PluginJobFailedPayload{
					PluginID:   pluginID,
					Name:       m.pluginDisplayName(context.Background(), pluginID),
					Job:        routePath,
					Kind:       "expand",
					Error:      reason,
					DurationMS: durMS,
				}, false)
			}
		} else {
			j.finish("done", "")
		}
	}()
	return true, nil
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.startActionJob

``````
// startActionJob runs owner-started work. At most ActionJobConcurrency owner or
// scheduled jobs and ResolverJobConcurrency resolver jobs run concurrently per
// plugin; at most sixteen route snapshots are retained per plugin.
func (m *Manager) startActionJob(pluginID string, body json.RawMessage) error {
	_, err := m.startResolverJob(pluginID, body, nil, "")
	return err
}

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.startResolverJob

``````
func (m *Manager) startResolverJob(pluginID string, body, initial json.RawMessage, suffix string) (*actionJob, error) {
	var out struct {
		Job string `json:"job"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(body, &out) != nil || out.Job == "" {
		return nil, nil
	}
	path := out.Job
	if !strings.HasPrefix(path, "/ether/job/") {
		path = "/ether/job/" + strings.TrimPrefix(path, "/")
	}
	if len(path) > 256 || strings.Contains(path, "..") || strings.ContainsAny(path, "?#\\") {
		return nil, nil
	}
	key := pluginID + "|" + path
	if suffix != "" {
		key = pluginID + "|resolver" + suffix
	}
	m.jobsMu.Lock()
	defer m.jobsMu.Unlock()
	if old, ok := m.jobs.Load(key); ok && old.(*actionJob).snapshot().State == "running" {
		return old.(*actionJob), nil
	}
	isResolver := suffix != ""
	resolverPrefix := pluginID + "|resolver|"
	hostPrefix := pluginID + "|host|"
	activeAction, activeResolver, count := 0, 0, 0
	oldestKey := ""
	var oldest time.Time
	m.jobs.Range(func(k, v any) bool {
		ks := k.(string)
		if !strings.HasPrefix(ks, pluginID+"|") {
			return true
		}
		s := v.(*actionJob).snapshot()
		if s.Code == frontendPreparationWaitCode {
			return true
		}
		count++
		if s.State == "running" {
			if strings.HasPrefix(ks, resolverPrefix) {
				activeResolver++
			} else if !strings.HasPrefix(ks, hostPrefix) {
				activeAction++
			}
		} else if oldestKey == "" || s.Started.Before(oldest) {
			oldestKey, oldest = ks, s.Started
		}
		return true
	})
	if !isResolver && activeAction >= ActionJobConcurrency {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("two background jobs are already running; wait for one to finish")
	}
	if isResolver && activeResolver >= ResolverJobConcurrency {
		msg := "Four playback preparation jobs are already running; wait for one to finish."
		refusedKey := pluginID + "|resolver:refused|" + path
		if _, exists := m.jobs.Load(refusedKey); !exists && count >= 16 && oldestKey != "" {
			m.jobs.Delete(oldestKey)
		}
		done := make(chan struct{})
		close(done)
		started := time.Now().UTC()
		if m.now != nil {
			started = m.now()
		}
		m.jobs.Store(refusedKey, &actionJob{
			cancel: func() {},
			done:   done,
			status: ActionJobStatus{
				Path:         path,
				State:        "error",
				Error:        msg,
				Started:      started,
				TotalLimitMS: m.runtimeCeilings(pluginID).deadline.Milliseconds(),
				AttemptLimit: ActionJobAttempts,
			},
		})
		m.log.Warn("plugins: resolver job refused", "plugin", pluginID, "job", path, "err", msg)
		return nil, &core.JobsBusyError{Message: msg}
	}
	if _, exists := m.jobs.Load(key); !exists && count >= 16 && oldestKey != "" {
		m.jobs.Delete(oldestKey)
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), m.runtimeCeilings(pluginID).deadline)
	j := &actionJob{cancel: cancel, done: make(chan struct{}), status: ActionJobStatus{Path: path, State: "running", Started: time.Now().UTC(), TotalLimitMS: m.runtimeCeilings(pluginID).deadline.Milliseconds(), AttemptLimit: ActionJobAttempts}}
	m.jobs.Store(key, j)
	go func() {
		runtime.LockOSThread() // Do not unlock: this lowered-priority thread is discarded on return.
		if !isResolver {
			// A resolver job prepares playback a viewer is waiting on:
			// it keeps normal priority and never waits for the server
			// to go idle (active streams would otherwise stall it).
			lowerJobPriority()
		}
		defer cancel()
		defer close(j.done)
		redact := func(s string) string {
			if m == nil || m.store == nil {
				return logredact.String(s)
			}
			return m.store.redactKnown(context.Background(), pluginID, s)
		}
		err := runActionJobWithHook(ctx, j, ActionJobAttempts, func(ctx context.Context, token json.RawMessage) (Response, error) {
			if !isResolver {
				if err := wasm.WaitBackground(ctx, m.deps.Busy); err != nil {
					return Response{}, err
				}
			}
			payload := map[string]json.RawMessage{}
			_ = json.Unmarshal(initial, &payload)
			if payload == nil {
				payload = map[string]json.RawMessage{}
			}
			if len(token) > 0 {
				payload["continuation"] = token
			}
			encoded, _ := json.Marshal(payload)
			callCtx := ctx
			if !isResolver {
				callCtx = WithBackgroundCall(ctx)
			}
			return m.Call(callCtx, pluginID, Request{Method: "POST", Path: path, Body: encoded, Foreground: isResolver})
		}, nil, redact)
		if err != nil {
			state := "error"
			if ctx.Err() == context.Canceled {
				state = "canceled"
			}
			if ctx.Err() == context.DeadlineExceeded {
				err = fmt.Errorf("job reached its total time limit of %s", m.runtimeCeilings(pluginID).deadline)
			}
			reason := m.store.redactKnown(context.Background(), pluginID, err.Error())
			j.finish(state, reason)
			m.log.Warn("plugins: action job", "plugin", pluginID, "job", path, "err", reason)
			if state == "error" {
				kind := "action"
				if isResolver {
					kind = "resolver"
				}
				durMS := max(time.Since(j.snapshot().Started).Milliseconds(), int64(0))
				m.emitBusEvent(events.EventPluginJobFailed, pluginID, events.PluginJobFailedPayload{
					PluginID:   pluginID,
					Name:       m.pluginDisplayName(context.Background(), pluginID),
					Job:        path,
					Kind:       kind,
					Error:      reason,
					DurationMS: durMS,
				}, false)
			}
		} else {
			j.finish("done", "")
		}
	}()
	return j, nil
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#runActionJob

``````
// runActionJob treats an absent continuation flag as completion for existing
// one-call jobs. Explicit failures and non-success HTTP responses always stop.
func runActionJob(ctx context.Context, j *actionJob, attempts int, call func(context.Context, json.RawMessage) (Response, error)) error {
	return runActionJobWithHook(ctx, j, attempts, call, nil, nil)
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#runActionJobWithHook

``````
func runActionJobWithHook(ctx context.Context, j *actionJob, attempts int, call func(context.Context, json.RawMessage) (Response, error), onStep func(json.RawMessage) error, redact func(string) string) error {
	var token json.RawMessage
	for n := 0; n < attempts; n++ {
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("job stopped: %w", err)
		}
		j.mu.Lock()
		j.status.Attempts++
		j.mu.Unlock()
		resp, err := call(ctx, token)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("job stopped: %w", err)
		}
		if resp.Status < 200 || resp.Status >= 300 {
			return formatJobHTTPError(resp.Status, resp.Body, redact)
		}
		var step struct {
			ContinueInMS *int64          `json:"continueInMs"`
			Continuation json.RawMessage `json:"continuation"`
			Progress     string          `json:"progress"`
			Done         bool            `json:"done"`
			Failed       string          `json:"failed"`
		}
		if len(resp.Body) > 0 {
			if err = json.Unmarshal(resp.Body, &step); err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("invalid job response: %w", err)
			}
		}
		if len(step.Progress) > 1024 {
			return fmt.Errorf("job progress exceeds 1024 bytes")
		}
		j.mu.Lock()
		if step.Progress != "" {
			j.status.Progress = step.Progress
		}
		j.mu.Unlock()
		if step.Failed != "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("job failed: %.1024s", step.Failed)
		}
		if onStep != nil && len(resp.Body) > 0 {
			if err := onStep(resp.Body); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		if step.Done || step.ContinueInMS == nil {
			return nil
		}
		if *step.ContinueInMS < 0 || *step.ContinueInMS > 300000 {
			return fmt.Errorf("continueInMs must be between 0 and 300000")
		}
		if len(step.Continuation) > 64<<10 {
			return fmt.Errorf("job continuation exceeds 64 KiB")
		}
		token = step.Continuation
		if n+1 == attempts {
			break
		}
		timer := time.NewTimer(max(actionJobMinDelay, time.Duration(*step.ContinueInMS)*time.Millisecond))
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			timer.Stop()
			return fmt.Errorf("job stopped: %w", ctx.Err())
		case <-timer.C:
		}
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("job reached its limit of %d calls", attempts)
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#summarizeJobErrorBody

``````
// summarizeJobErrorBody extracts a bounded, single-line, secret-redacted
// summary from a non-2xx plugin job response body (preferring a structured
// message field when present). Redaction runs before truncation so a secret
// straddling the truncation boundary is never partially exposed (#768).
func summarizeJobErrorBody(body json.RawMessage, redact func(string) string) string {
	raw := unwrapJSONStringBody(body)
	if len(raw) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	const maxInspectBytes = 64 << 10
	if len(raw) > maxInspectBytes {
		raw = raw[:maxInspectBytes]
	}
	var text string
	var env struct {
		Error   json.RawMessage `json:"error"`
		Message string          `json:"message"`
		Failed  string          `json:"failed"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(raw, &env) == nil {
		var errStr string
		if len(env.Error) > 0 {
			var errObj struct {
				Message string `json:"message"`
			}
			if json.Unmarshal(env.Error, &errObj) == nil && strings.TrimSpace(errObj.Message) != "" {
				text = errObj.Message
			} else {
				_ = json.Unmarshal(env.Error, &errStr)
			}
		}
		if text == "" && strings.TrimSpace(env.Message) != "" {
			text = env.Message
		}
		if text == "" && strings.TrimSpace(env.Failed) != "" {
			text = env.Failed
		}
		if text == "" && strings.TrimSpace(errStr) != "" {
			text = errStr
		}
	}
	if text == "" {
		if scrubbed := redactJSON(raw); scrubbed != "" {
			text = scrubbed
		} else {
			text = string(raw)
		}
	}
	if redact != nil {
		text = redact(text)
	}
	text = logredact.String(text)
	text = strings.Join(strings.Fields(text), " ")
	if text == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return truncate(text, jobErrorBodyLimit)
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#formatJobHTTPError

``````
func formatJobHTTPError(status int, body json.RawMessage, redact func(string) string) error {
	if summary := summarizeJobErrorBody(body, redact); summary != "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("job returned HTTP %d: %s", status, summary)
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("job returned HTTP %d", status)
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.cancelActionJobs

``````
func (m *Manager) cancelActionJobs(id string) {
	var flights []*scheduleFlight
	m.mu.Lock()
	for k, f := range m.scheduleInFlight {
		if id == "" || strings.HasPrefix(k, id+"|") {
			flights = append(flights, f)
			delete(m.scheduleInFlight, k)
		}
	}
	for k := range m.scheduleJobs {
		if id == "" || strings.HasPrefix(k, id+"|") {
			delete(m.scheduleJobs, k)
		}
	}
	m.mu.Unlock()
	for _, f := range flights {
		f.cancel()
	}
	m.jobs.Range(func(k, v any) bool {
		if id == "" || strings.HasPrefix(k.(string), id+"|") {
			v.(*actionJob).cancel()
		}
		return true
	})
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.handleActionJobs

``````
func (m *Manager) handleActionJobs(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	id := r.PathValue("id")
	if _, err := m.Get(r.Context(), id); err != nil {
		m.fail(w, err)
		return
	}
	jobs := []ActionJobStatus{}
	m.jobs.Range(func(k, v any) bool {
		if strings.HasPrefix(k.(string), id+"|") {
			s := v.(*actionJob).snapshot()
			if s.Code == frontendPreparationWaitCode {
				s.Label = frontend.PluginPreparationLabel(r.Header.Get("Accept-Language"))
			}
			s.Progress = m.store.redactKnown(r.Context(), id, s.Progress)
			s.Outcome = m.store.redactKnown(r.Context(), id, s.Outcome)
			s.Error = m.store.redactKnown(r.Context(), id, s.Error)
			jobs = append(jobs, s)
		}
		return true
	})
	sort.Slice(jobs, func(i, j int) bool { return jobs[i].Started.After(jobs[j].Started) })
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, jobs)
}
``````

## Source: internal/plugins/action_jobs.go#*Manager.handleCancelActionJob

``````
func (m *Manager) handleCancelActionJob(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req struct {
		Path string `json:"path"`
	}
	if err := decode(r, &req); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, "invalid", "The request was not understood.", nil)
		return
	}
	m.jobs.Range(func(k, v any) bool {
		if strings.HasPrefix(k.(string), r.PathValue("id")+"|") && v.(*actionJob).snapshot().Path == req.Path {
			v.(*actionJob).cancel()
		}
		return true
	})
	writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]bool{"ok": true})
}
``````
